sentences.zh: 高永年，河東蕃官也。

translations.literal: Gao Yongnian was a tribal official of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yongnian was a tribal officer from Hedong.

sentences.zh: 為麟州都巡檢。

translations.literal: He served as chief inspector of Lin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He served as chief inspector of Lin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 王贍取青唐，永年總蕃兵為先鋒。

translations.literal: When Wang Zhan captured Qingtang, Yongnian commanded tribal troops as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Zhan took Qingtang, Yongnian led tribal forces in the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 贍入邈川，而宗哥叛，永年以千騎直抵其城，開省章峽路，擊走叛羌，結陣還青唐。

translations.literal: Zhan entered Miaochuan, but Zongge rebelled; Yongnian with a thousand horsemen went straight to his city, opened the Shengzhang Gorge route, drove off the rebel Qiang, formed ranks, and returned to Qingtang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan entered Miaochuan while Zongge rebelled. Yongnian rode a thousand men straight to the rebel city, opened the Shengzhang Gorge road, beat back the Qiang, re-formed his line, and withdrew to Qingtang.

sentences.zh: 羌攻甚急，復擊之去。

translations.literal: The Qiang pressed the attack fiercely; he struck them again and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: The Qiang pressed hard; he attacked again and drove them away.

sentences.zh: 會苗履、姚雄以援師至，戰溪蘭宗堡，履少卻，永年領勁騎斷羌為二，乃退。

translations.literal: When Miao Lü and Yao Xiong arrived with relief, they fought at Xilan Zong Fort; Lü fell back slightly, and Yongnian led crack cavalry to cut the Qiang in two, then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Relief under Miao Lü and Yao Xiong reached them at Xilan Zong Fort. When Lü gave ground, Yongnian led elite horsemen to split the Qiang force in two and then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 復與李克保敦穀，又戰於乾溝，單馬援矛，刺羌酋彪雞廝萬眾之中，斬其首，餘眾宵遁。

translations.literal: Again with Li Ke he held Dun Valley, and fought again at Qian Gully; alone on horseback he thrust with his spear and in the midst of ten thousand men stabbed the Qiang chief Biaoji, cut off his head, and the rest fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: He fought again with Li Ke at Dun Valley and at Qian Gully. Alone on horseback he drove his spear through the Qiang chief Biaoji amid ten thousand men, took his head, and the rest fled overnight.

sentences.zh: 已而隴拶自乾溝逼鄯州，永年佐贍拒守，及雄棄湟、鄯，皆以永年殿歸師。

translations.literal: Later Longzan advanced from Qian Gully against Shazhou; Yongnian aided Zhan in defense, and when Xiong abandoned Huang and Shazhou, Yongnian covered the army on its retreat.
translations.idiomatic: When Longzan later pressed Shazhou from Qian Gully, Yongnian helped Zhan hold the line; and when Xiong abandoned Huang and Shazhou, Yongnian brought up the rear on every withdrawal.

sentences.zh: 崇寧初，知岷州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chongning, he was made prefect of Minzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Chongning era he was appointed prefect of Minzhou.

sentences.zh: 蔡京議復兩州，王厚使永年帥兵二萬出京玉關，克安川堡，遂至湟，即知州事。

translations.literal: Cai Jing planned to recover the two prefectures; Wang Hou had Yongnian lead twenty thousand men out through Jingyu Pass, took Anchuan Fort, and reached Huang, where he assumed prefectural duties.
translations.idiomatic: When Cai Jing sought to recover the two prefectures, Wang Hou sent Yongnian with twenty thousand men through Jingyu Pass. They took Anchuan Fort, reached Huang, and Yongnian took charge of the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 自皇城副使進四方館使、利州刺史，為熙、秦兩路兵都統製，將前軍駐宗哥北。

translations.literal: Promoted from deputy commissioner of the Imperial City to envoy of the Four Directions Hall and prefect of Lizhou, he became overall commander of troops on the Xi and Qin circuits, with the forward army stationed north of Zongge.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from deputy commissioner of the Imperial City to envoy of the Four Directions Hall and prefect of Lizhou, and was made overall commander of Xi and Qin forces, with the vanguard encamped north of Zongge.

sentences.zh: 溪賒羅撒萃精勇據高阜，欲衝官軍，永年揮選鋒突陣，師乘之，羌大敗，遂平鄯州。

translations.literal: Xisheluosuo gathered picked warriors on a high ridge to charge the government army; Yongnian waved the assault troops into the line, the army followed, the Qiang were routed, and Shazhou was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Xisheluosuo massed elite fighters on high ground to break the imperial line. Yongnian sent the assault corps into the array, the main force followed, the Qiang were shattered, and Shazhou was taken.

sentences.zh: 遷賀州團練使，知其州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to regimental commander of He Prefecture and continued as its prefect.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to regimental commander of He Prefecture and retained the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 溪賒羅撒合夏國四監軍之眾，逼宣威城，永年出禦之。

translations.literal: Xisheluosuo combined the forces of four Xia supervisory armies and pressed Xuancheng, and Yongnian went out to meet them.
translations.idiomatic: Xisheluosuo united four Xia supervisory armies against Xuancheng, and Yongnian marched out to oppose them.

sentences.zh: 行三十里，逢羌帳下親兵，皆永年昔所推納熟戶也。

translations.literal: After thirty li he met personal guards from the Qiang camp—all households Yongnian had once sponsored and settled.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty li out he met Qiang guards from the enemy camp, all tribesmen he had once brought in and settled.

sentences.zh: 永年不之備，羌遽執永年以叛，遂為多羅巴所殺，探其心肝食之，謂其下曰：「此人奪我國，使吾宗族漂落無處所，不可不殺也。」

translations.literal: Yongnian was unprepared; the Qiang seized him at once and rebelled. Duoluoba killed him, took out his heart and liver and ate them, and said to his men: “This man seized our country and left our clans adrift with nowhere to go—we must kill him.”
translations.idiomatic: Unprepared, Yongnian was seized and turned over to the rebels. Duoluoba killed him, ate his heart and liver, and told his men: “This man took our country and scattered our kin—we could not spare him.”

sentences.zh: 是役也，王厚實主其事，而謀策皆出永年，乃劾永年信任降羌，坐受執縛，故贈恤不及雲。

translations.literal: In that campaign Wang Hou nominally led, but the plans all came from Yongnian; yet he was impeached for trusting surrendered Qiang and allowing himself to be seized, so posthumous honors did not match his service.
translations.idiomatic: In that campaign Wang Hou held nominal command while Yongnian devised the strategy; yet Yongnian was impeached for trusting surrendered Qiang and being captured, and his rewards fell short.

sentences.zh: 永年略知文義，範純仁嘗令贄所著書詣闕，作《元符隴右錄》，不以棄湟、鄯為是，故蔡京用之，雖成功，然竟以此死雲。

translations.literal: Yongnian had some literary learning; Fan Chunren once had him present his writings at court. He wrote 《Records of Longyou in the Yuanfu Era》 and did not approve abandoning Huang and Shazhou, so Cai Jing used him; though he succeeded, he died for it in the end.
translations.idiomatic: Yongnian knew some letters. Fan Chunren once had him present his writings at court; his 《Records of Longyou in the Yuanfu Era》 opposed abandoning Huang and Shazhou, which is why Cai Jing employed him—and why success still ended in his death.

sentences.zh: 鞠嗣復，不知何許人。

translations.literal: Ju Sifu—his origin is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Ju Sifu’s birthplace is not recorded.

sentences.zh: 宣和初，知歙州休寧縣。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xuanhe he was magistrate of Xiuning County in She Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xuanhe he governed Xiuning County in She Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 方臘黨破縣，欲逼使降，麵斬二士以怖之，嗣復罵曰：「自古妖賊豈有長久者，爾當去逆從順，因我而歸朝，官爵尚可得，何為脅我使降？」

translations.literal: When Fang La’s band broke the county and tried to force him to surrender, they beheaded two scholars before him to terrify him. Sifu cursed them: “Since antiquity, have demonic rebels ever lasted long? You should cast off rebellion and follow the right, return to the court through me, and rank and office may still be yours—why threaten me to surrender?”
translations.idiomatic: Fang La’s rebels took the county and tried to force his surrender, beheading two scholars to frighten him. Sifu cursed them: “Rebels like you never endure. Turn back, follow the throne through me, and you may yet keep rank—why threaten me?”

sentences.zh: 嗣復知必死，不少懾，屢言何不速殺我，賊曰：「我，縣人也。

translations.literal: Sifu knew he must die and showed no fear, repeatedly crying why they did not kill him at once. The bandits said: “I am a man of this county.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing he would die, he showed no fear and kept asking why they delayed. One rebel said: “I am from this county.

sentences.zh: 明府宰邑有善政，我不忍殺。」

translations.literal: The magistrate has governed well; I cannot bear to kill him.”
translations.idiomatic: You have ruled us well; I cannot kill you.”

sentences.zh: 乃委之而去。

translations.literal: They left him and went away.
translations.idiomatic: They released him and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 初，嗣復聞難，率吏民修城立門，眾赴功，守備略就。

translations.literal: When trouble first arose, Sifu had led clerks and people to repair the walls and gates; the crowd came to work and defenses were largely ready.
translations.idiomatic: At the first alarm he had clerks and townspeople repair walls and gates; many came to help and the defenses were nearly ready.

sentences.zh: 朝廷知之，進其官二等，加直秘閣，擢知睦州。

translations.literal: The court learned of it, advanced his rank two steps, added appointment to the Direct Secretariat, and promoted him to prefect of Mu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The court advanced him two ranks, added the Direct Secretariat, and made him prefect of Mu.

sentences.zh: 嘗為賊所傷，自力度江乞師於宣撫使，未及行而卒。

translations.literal: Once wounded by bandits, he crossed the river himself to beg troops from the pacification commissioner but died before he could set out.
translations.idiomatic: Wounded by rebels, he crossed the river to beg troops from the pacification commissioner and died before he could march.

sentences.zh: 宋旅字庭實，莆田人。

translations.literal: Song Lu, style Tingshi, was a man of Putian.
translations.idiomatic: Song Lu, style name Tingshi, was from Putian.

sentences.zh: 第進士，累官奉議郎、知剡縣。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and rose to Gentleman for Court Discussion and magistrate of Shan County.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi, he rose to Gentleman for Court Discussion and magistrate of Shan County.

sentences.zh: 方臘既陷歙、睦、杭、衢、婺五州，且犯越，越盜亦起應之。

translations.literal: After Fang La had taken She, Mu, Hang, Qu, and Wu prefectures and was about to invade Yue, local bandits in Yue also rose in response.
translations.idiomatic: When Fang La had seized five prefectures and threatened Yue, bandits there rose in answer.

sentences.zh: 縣吏多遁，旅遣妻子浮海歸閩，獨與民據守，以忠義激勸，部勒隊伍，為豫備計。

translations.literal: Most county clerks fled; Lu sent wife and children by sea back to Min and alone held the city with the people, rousing them with loyalty and righteousness, drilling companies, and making ready.
translations.idiomatic: Clerks fled; Lu sent his family home by sea and held the county alone, stirring the people with talk of duty, drilling troops, and preparing defense.

sentences.zh: 俄而盜眾大至，射率壯銳，冒矢石，雖頗殺獲，終以力不敵，遂死之。

translations.literal: Soon a great host came; he led the brave through arrow and stone. Though they killed many, strength failed at last and he died.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels came in force he led the stoutest men under fire. They killed many, but were overwhelmed and he fell.

sentences.zh: 越帥劉韐上其事，詔贈朝散郎，錄其四子。

translations.literal: Liu Kai, military commissioner of Yue, reported it; the throne posthumously made him Gentleman for Spreading Morality and enrolled four sons.
translations.idiomatic: The Yue commander Liu Kai reported his death; the court posthumously made him Gentleman for Spreading Morality and enrolled four sons.

sentences.zh: 丁仲修字敏之，溫州人。

translations.literal: Ding Zhongxiu, style Minzhi, was a man of Wenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Zhongxiu, style Minzhi, was from Wenzhou.

sentences.zh: 方臘黨俞道安陷樂清，將渡江。

translations.literal: Fang La’s follower Yu Dao’an took Yueqing and was about to cross the river.
translations.idiomatic: Fang La’s man Yu Dao’an seized Yueqing and prepared to cross the river.

sentences.zh: 巡檢陳華往捕，死之。

translations.literal: Inspector Chen Hua went to seize him and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector Chen Hua went to capture him and died.

sentences.zh: 先鋒將張理同、李振出南門迎敵，渡八接橋，橋斷馬蹶，溺死。

translations.literal: Vanguard generals Zhang Litong and Li Zhen went out the south gate to meet the enemy; crossing Bajie Bridge, the bridge broke, horses stumbled, and they drowned.
translations.idiomatic: Vanguards Zhang Litong and Li Zhen met the enemy at the south gate; at Bajie Bridge the span gave way, horses fell, and both drowned.

sentences.zh: 賊至帆遊，夏祥遣輔褒迎戰數十合，褒死之。

translations.literal: When bandits reached Fanyou, Xia Xiang sent Fu Bao to fight dozens of rounds; Bao died.
translations.idiomatic: At Fanyou, Xia Xiang sent Fu Bao to fight many rounds until Bao fell.

sentences.zh: 仲修帥鄉兵禦諸樂灣，鄉兵失據而散，仲修以餘兵與賊戰，力屈乃死。

translations.literal: Zhongxiu led militia at Yue Bay; the militia lost position and scattered; with the remnant he fought the bandits until strength failed and he died.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxiu led militia at Yue Bay; when they broke he fought on with the remnant until he was killed.

sentences.zh: 項德，婺州武義人，郡之禁卒也。

translations.literal: Xiang De, a man of Wuyi in Wu Prefecture, was a garrison soldier of the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang De of Wuyi in Wu Prefecture was a commandery garrison soldier.

sentences.zh: 宣和間，盜發幫源，明年陷婺，而邑隨沒。

translations.literal: In Xuanhe bandits rose at Bangyuan; the next year they took Wu, and the county fell with it.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuanhe rebels rose at Bangyuan; the next year Wu fell and his county with it.

sentences.zh: 德率敗亡百人破賊，因據邑之城隍祠。

translations.literal: De led a hundred scattered men to break the bandits and held the city-god shrine within the walls.
translations.idiomatic: De rallied a hundred survivors, routed the rebels, and held the city-god shrine inside the walls.

sentences.zh: 自二月訖五月，東抗江蔡，西拒董奉，北捍王國，大小百餘戰，出則居選鋒之先，入則殿後，前後俘馘不可勝計。

translations.literal: From the second month to the fifth he fought east against Jiang Cai, west against Dong Feng, and north against Wang Guo—more than a hundred battles large and small; in attack he led the assault, in retreat he brought up the rear, and captives taken were beyond count.
translations.idiomatic: From the second to the fifth month he fought Jiang Cai in the east, Dong Feng in the west, and Wang Guo in the north—over a hundred battles; he led every assault and covered every retreat, and captives were countless.

sentences.zh: 賊目為「項鷂子」，聞其鉦則相率遁去。

translations.literal: Bandits called him “Xiang the Kite”; at the sound of his gong they fled together.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels named him “Xiang the Kite”; at his gong they scattered.

sentences.zh: 方謀復永康諸縣，而官兵至，德引其眾欲會合，賊盡銳邀之黃姑嶺下，德戰死。

translations.literal: As he planned to recover Yongkang and other counties, government troops arrived; he led his men to join them, but bandits ambushed him in force at Huanggu Ridge and De died fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Planning to recover Yongkang, he marched to join government troops; rebels waylaid him at Huanggu Ridge and he died fighting.

sentences.zh: 邑人哭聲震山谷，圖其像，歲時祭之。

translations.literal: The people’s wailing shook the valleys; they painted his likeness and sacrificed to it each year.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning shook the valleys; they painted his image and sacrificed yearly.

sentences.zh: 孫昭遠，字顯叔，其先眉州眉山人。

translations.literal: Sun Zhaoyuan, style Xianshu, was descended from Meizhou in Meizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Zhaoyuan, style Xianshu, came from Meizhou.

sentences.zh: 元祐間進士，調長沙尉，辟河東經略司幹當公事。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the Yuanyou era, he was appointed sheriff of Changsha and entered the Hedong military commission as clerk.
translations.idiomatic: A Yuanyou jinshi, he became sheriff of Changsha and clerk on the Hedong commission.

sentences.zh: 曆鳳翔府天興縣、河北山東撫諭盜賊幹當公事，尋擢河北、燕山府路轉運使。

translations.literal: He served Tianxing County in Fengxiang Prefecture and as clerk for pacifying bandits in Hebei and Shandong, then rose to transport commissioner on the Hebei and Yanshan circuits.
translations.idiomatic: He served in Tianxing, pacified bandits in Hebei and Shandong, then became transport commissioner for Hebei and Yanshan.

sentences.zh: 靖康元年，召為水部員外郎。

translations.literal: In Jingkang 1 he was summoned as Vice Director of the Water Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingkang 1 he was summoned as Vice Director of the Water Bureau.

sentences.zh: 金人圍太原，宋師多潰，欽宗遣折彥質乘傳同昭遠招集。

translations.literal: The Jurchens besieged Taiyuan; Song forces largely broke; Emperor Qinzong sent Zhe Yanzhi by post to gather troops with Zhaoyuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Taiyuan was besieged and Song forces broke, Qinzong sent Zhe Yanzhi to gather troops with Zhaoyuan.

sentences.zh: 會洛陽陷，西京留守、西道總管王襄徙治襄、漢，授昭遠西道總管。

translations.literal: When Luoyang fell, Western Capital custodian and western-route overall commander Wang Xiang moved his seat to Xiang and Han and appointed Zhaoyuan overall commander of the western route.
translations.idiomatic: When Luoyang fell, Wang Xiang moved west and made Zhaoyuan commander of the western route.

sentences.zh: 道收潰卒至京兆，遇永興路安撫范致虛會諸軍入援，昭遠督其進，且檄諸道使出師。

translations.literal: On the road he gathered broken troops to Jingzhao, met Yongxing pacifier Fan Zhixu assembling armies to relieve the capital, urged them forward, and ordered commissioners of all routes to march.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered broken troops to Jingzhao, met Fan Zhixu leading relief armies, urged them forward, and ordered all routes to march.

sentences.zh: 環慶帥王似、熙河帥王倚各以師會，涇原帥席貢、秦鳳帥趙點、鄜坊使張深皆後師期，昭遠二十有八疏劾之。

translations.literal: Huanqing commander Wang Si and Xihe commander Wang Yi each brought troops to join; Jingyuan commander Xi Gong, Qinfeng commander Zhao Dian, and Bian-Fang commissioner Zhang Shen all missed the rendezvous, and Zhaoyuan impeached them in twenty-eight memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Si and Wang Yi brought troops, but Xi Gong, Zhao Dian, and Zhang Shen were late; Zhaoyuan impeached them in twenty-eight memorials.

sentences.zh: 合諸道兵得十萬，命馬祐昌統之。

translations.literal: Combining troops from all routes he mustered one hundred thousand and ordered Ma Youchang to command them.
translations.idiomatic: He mustered one hundred thousand men from all routes and put Ma Youchang in command.

sentences.zh: 昭遠與致虛同出關，祐昌與金人戰敗。

translations.literal: Zhaoyuan and Zhixu went out through the pass together; Youchang was defeated fighting the Jurchens.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoyuan and Fan Zhixu marched out together; Ma Youchang was defeated.

sentences.zh: 京師陷，遣使至大元帥府。

translations.literal: When the capital fell he sent envoys to the Grand Marshal’s headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital fell he sent envoys to the Grand Marshal’s headquarters.

sentences.zh: 建炎元年，遷河南尹、西京留守、西道都總管。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianyan he was made Intendant of Henan, Western Capital custodian, and overall commander of the western route.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianyan 1 he became Intendant of Henan, custodian of the Western Capital, and commander of the western route.

sentences.zh: 至洛收集散亡，得義兵萬餘人，柵伊陽，使民入保。

translations.literal: Reaching Luoyang he gathered the scattered and mustered more than ten thousand volunteers, palisaded Yiyang, and had the people enter for protection.
translations.idiomatic: At Luoyang he gathered refugees and more than ten thousand volunteers, fortified Yiyang, and sheltered the people.

sentences.zh: 其冬，金人來攻，昭遠遣將姚慶拒戰，軍敗，慶死。

translations.literal: That winter the Jurchens attacked; Zhaoyuan sent General Yao Qing to resist; the army was beaten and Qing died.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the Jurchens attacked; he sent Yao Qing to resist; the army was defeated and Qing killed.

sentences.zh: 昭遠命將官王仔奉啟運諸殿神御，間道走行在。

translations.literal: Zhaoyuan ordered Officer Wang Zai to escort the imperial spirit tablets of the halls by a hidden route to the mobile court.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Wang Zai to escort the imperial spirit tablets by a hidden route to the court in exile.

sentences.zh: 金兵益熾，昭遠戰不利，其下欲擁昭遠南還，昭遠罵曰：「若等平日衣食縣官，不以此時報國，南去何為！」

translations.literal: As Jurchen pressure grew and battle went ill, his men wished to escort Zhaoyuan south. He cursed them: “You daily eat the state’s grain—will you not repay it now? Why go south!”
translations.idiomatic: Battle turned against him and his men wanted to carry him south. He raged: “You live on the state’s grain—will you not repay it now? Why flee south!”

sentences.zh: 叛兵怒，反擊昭遠，遂遇害。

translations.literal: The mutineers were enraged, turned on Zhaoyuan, and he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Mutineers turned on him and killed him.

sentences.zh: 官屬無免者。

translations.literal: No official escaped.
translations.idiomatic: No member of his staff survived.

sentences.zh: 四年，追贈徽猷閣待制。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was posthumously made Attendant-in-Waiting of the Hall of Imperial Sagacity.
translations.idiomatic: In year four he was posthumously made Attendant-in-Waiting of the Hall of Imperial Sagacity.

sentences.zh: 曾孝序，字逢原，泉州晉江人。

translations.literal: Ceng Xiaoxu, style Fengyuan, was a man of Jinjiang in Quan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Ceng Xiaoxu, style Fengyuan, was from Jinjiang in Quan.

sentences.zh: 以蔭補將作監主簿，監泰州海安鹽倉，因家泰州。

translations.literal: By yin privilege he became chief clerk of the Directorate of Works, supervised the Haian salt depot in Taizhou, and made his home there.
translations.idiomatic: By yin privilege he entered the Directorate of Works, supervised the Haian salt depot in Taizhou, and settled there.

sentences.zh: 累官至環慶路經略、安撫使。

translations.literal: He rose to military commissioner and pacification commissioner of Huanqing Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to military commissioner and pacifier of Huanqing Circuit.

sentences.zh: 過闕，與蔡京論講議司事，曰：「天下之財貴於流通，取民膏血以聚京師，恐非太平法。」

translations.literal: Passing the capital he debated the Bureau of Policy Discussion with Cai Jing, saying: “The empire’s wealth lies in circulation; draining the people’s blood to heap up the capital is hardly the way of peace.”
translations.idiomatic: At court he told Cai Jing: “Wealth must circulate; squeezing the people dry for the capital is no policy of peace.”

sentences.zh: 京銜之。

translations.literal: Jing bore a grudge.
translations.idiomatic: Jing resented it.

sentences.zh: 時京方行結糴、俵糴之法，盡括民財充數，孝序上疏曰：「民力殫矣。

translations.literal: Jing was then enforcing tied purchase and loaned-grain schemes, scraping all private wealth to fill quotas. Xiaoxu memorialized: “The people’s strength is exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: While Jing forced tied purchase and loaned-grain schemes, Xiaoxu wrote: “The people are spent.

sentences.zh: 民為邦本，一有逃移，誰與守邦？」

translations.literal: The people are the root of the state; once they flee, who will guard it?”
translations.idiomatic: The people are the state’s root; when they flee, who will defend it?”

sentences.zh: 京益怒，遣御史宋聖寵劾其私事，追逮其家人，鍛煉無所得，但言約日出師，幾誤軍期，削籍竄嶺表。

translations.literal: Jing grew angrier, sent the censor Song Shengchong to impeach him on private grounds, seized his family, tortured them without result, and only charged that he had fixed a day to march and nearly missed the campaign—stripped of registry and exiled to the far south.
translations.idiomatic: Jing sent Song Shengchong to impeach him, seized his family, tortured them in vain, then punished him for nearly missing a march date—stripped of rank and exiled south.

sentences.zh: 遇赦，量移永州。

translations.literal: On an amnesty he was transferred to Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Amnestied, he was moved to Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 京罷相，授顯謨閣待制、知潭州。

translations.literal: When Jing left office, Xiaoxu was made Attendant-in-Waiting of the Hall of Manifest Counsel and prefect of Tan.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing fell, Xiaoxu was made Attendant of the Hall of Manifest Counsel and prefect of Tan.

sentences.zh: 復以論徭事與吳居厚不合，落職知袁州，尋復職，再知潭州。

translations.literal: Again he clashed with Wu Ju over Yao affairs, was demoted to Yuan, soon restored, and again governed Tan.
translations.idiomatic: He clashed with Wu Ju over Yao affairs, was demoted to Yuan, restored, and again governed Tan.

sentences.zh: 道州徭人叛，乘高恃險，機毒矢下射，官軍不得前，於兩山間仆巨木，橫累以守。

translations.literal: Yao rebels in Da Prefecture held the heights, shot poisoned arrows so troops could not advance, and felled great trees between the mountains to bar the way.
translations.idiomatic: Yao in Da held the heights, rained poisoned arrows, and felled trees across the passes.

sentences.zh: 孝序夜遣驍銳攀援而上，以大兵繼進，破平之。

translations.literal: Xiaoxu sent picked men by night to climb up; the main force followed and crushed them.
translations.idiomatic: He sent night climbers, followed with the main army, and crushed them.

sentences.zh: 進顯謨閣直學士，遷龍圖閣直學士、知青州。

translations.literal: Promoted to Direct Academician of the Hall of Manifest Counsel, he became Direct Academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall and prefect of Qing.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted, he became Direct Academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall and prefect of Qing.

sentences.zh: 繕修城池，訓練士卒，儲峙金穀，有數年之備，金人不敢犯。

translations.literal: He repaired walls, trained soldiers, stored grain and gold, prepared for years, and the Jurchens did not dare attack.
translations.idiomatic: He rebuilt walls, trained troops, stored grain and gold for years of siege, and the Jurchens did not attack.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，遷徽猷閣學士，升延康殿學士，召赴行在。

translations.literal: When Gaozong took the throne, Xiaoxu was made Academician of the Hall of Imperial Sagacity, then of the Hall of Extended Glory, and summoned to the mobile court.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong made him Academician of the Hall of Imperial Sagacity, then Extended Glory, and summoned him to court.

sentences.zh: 既而青州民詣南都借留，許之。

translations.literal: Then Qing people went to the southern capital to beg he stay; this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Qing people begged the court to keep him; the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 先是，臨朐土兵趙晟聚眾為亂，孝序付將官王定兵千人捕之，失利而歸。

translations.literal: Earlier the militia leader Zhao Sheng of Linqu had gathered a mob; Xiaoxu gave Officer Wang Ding a thousand men to seize him; they failed and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Zhao Sheng of Linqu had raised a mob; Xiaoxu sent Wang Ding with a thousand men, who failed and returned.

sentences.zh: 孝序責以力戰自贖，定乃以言撼敗卒，奪門斬關入，孝序出據廳事，瞋目罵之，遂與其子宣教郎訏皆遇害，年七十九。

translations.literal: Xiaoxu ordered him to redeem himself in fierce fighting; Ding stirred the beaten troops, broke the gate, and entered. Xiaoxu came out to the hall, glared and cursed him, and he and his son Xun, Instructor of the Court, were both killed—aged seventy-nine.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoxu told Ding to redeem himself in battle; Ding roused broken troops, stormed the gate, and entered. Xiaoxu cursed him from the hall; he and his son Xun were killed—he was seventy-nine.

sentences.zh: 城無主，遂陷。

translations.literal: With no one to lead, the city fell.
translations.idiomatic: Leaderless, the city fell.

sentences.zh: 知臨淄縣陸有常率民兵拒守，死於陣。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Linzi Lu Youchang led militia to resist and died in the line.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Youchang, magistrate of Linzi, led militia in defense and fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 知益都縣張侃、千乘縣丞丁興宗亦死之。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Yidu Zhang Kan and aide of Qiansheng Ding Xingzong also died.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Kan of Yidu and Ding Xingzong, aide of Qiansheng, died as well.

sentences.zh: 後贈孝序五官，為光祿大夫，諡威湣；

translations.literal: Later Xiaoxu was posthumously advanced five ranks, made Grandee of Splendid Happiness, with posthumous name Weimin;
translations.idiomatic: Later Xiaoxu was raised five ranks posthumously, made Grandee of Splendid Happiness, and given the posthumous name Weimin;

sentences.zh: 子訏承議郎。

translations.literal: his son Xun was made Gentleman for Discussion.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xun was made Gentleman for Discussion.

sentences.zh: 有常朝散郎，錄其家一人。

translations.literal: Youchang was made Gentleman for Spreading Morality; one person in his family was enrolled.
translations.idiomatic: Youchang was made Gentleman for Spreading Morality, and one kinsman was given office.

sentences.zh: 贈侃、興宗二官，官二子。

translations.literal: Kan and Xingzong were each advanced two ranks; two sons were given office.
translations.idiomatic: Kan and Xingzong were each advanced two ranks, and two sons were enrolled.

sentences.zh: 趙伯振，太祖八世孫。

translations.literal: Zhao Bozhen was an eighth-generation descendant of Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Bozhen was Taizu’s eighth-generation descendant.

sentences.zh: 宣和六年進士。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Xuanhe he passed the jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi in Xuanhe 6.

sentences.zh: 靖康末，為鄭州司錄，捍禦有功。

translations.literal: At the end of Jingkang he was recorder of Zheng Prefecture and distinguished himself in defense.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Jingkang he was recorder of Zheng and distinguished himself in defense.

sentences.zh: 上聞之，就遷直秘閣、通判州事。

translations.literal: The throne heard of it and promoted him to Direct Secretariat and vice-prefect of the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The court made him of the Direct Secretariat and vice-prefect of Zheng.

sentences.zh: 建炎元年，金人犯鄭州，守臣董庠棄城走。

translations.literal: In Jianyan 1 the Jurchens attacked Zheng; the prefect Dong Xiu abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianyan 1 the Jurchens attacked Zheng; Prefect Dong Xiu fled.

sentences.zh: 越八日城陷，伯振率兵巷戰，中流矢墜馬，遂遇害。

translations.literal: Eight days later the city fell; Bozhen led troops in street fighting, was struck by an arrow and fell from his horse, and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Eight days later the city fell. Bozhen fought in the streets, was struck by an arrow, fell from his horse, and died.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈朝請大夫，官其一子。

translations.literal: When reported, he was posthumously made Grandee for Court Audience and one son was given office.
translations.idiomatic: The court posthumously made him Grandee for Court Audience and enrolled one son.

sentences.zh: 王士言，武舉進士。

translations.literal: Wang Shiyan was a military-examination jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shiyan was a military-examination jinshi.

sentences.zh: 累立戰功，西北服其威名。

translations.literal: He repeatedly won battle merit and the northwest respected his renown.
translations.idiomatic: He won repeated battle honors and was famed in the northwest.

sentences.zh: 宣和初，擢河東廉訪使者。

translations.literal: Early in Xuanhe he was promoted to Hedong investigation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xuanhe he became Hedong investigation commissioner.

sentences.zh: 方臘為寇，詔擇材略之士，馮熙載薦為東南第三將，首解嘉興之圍。

translations.literal: When Fang La rebelled the court sought men of talent; Feng Xizai recommended him as Third Commander of the Southeast, and he first lifted the siege of Jiaxing.
translations.idiomatic: When Fang La rebelled, Feng Xizai recommended him as Third Commander of the Southeast, and he first lifted the siege of Jiaxing.

sentences.zh: 靖康元年，詔以浙西兵往河東防秋。

translations.literal: In Jingkang 1 he was ordered to take Zhexi troops to Hedong for autumn defense.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingkang 1 he was ordered to take Zhexi troops to defend Hedong in autumn.

sentences.zh: 金人攻澤州，畢力守禦，金兵日增，士言分必死。

translations.literal: The Jurchens attacked Ze Prefecture; he defended with all his strength; Jurchen numbers grew daily and Shiyan resolved to die.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jurchens attacked Ze he defended with all his strength; as their numbers grew he resolved to die.

sentences.zh: 他將力屈，城西南遂陷，乃使親卒持劍歸報，巷戰而死。

translations.literal: Other commanders gave way and the southwest of the city fell; he sent a trusted soldier with a sword to report back and died fighting in the lanes.
translations.idiomatic: When other defenders gave way and the southwest fell, he sent a trusted soldier to report and died fighting in the streets.

sentences.zh: 康允之上其事，贈拱衛大夫、忠州團練使，官其後五人。

translations.literal: Kang Yunzhi reported the affair; he was posthumously made Grandee of the Palace Guard and regimental commissioner of Zhong Prefecture, and five descendants were given office.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Yunzhi reported his death; he was posthumously made Grandee of the Palace Guard and regimental commissioner of Zhong, and five kinsmen were enrolled.

sentences.zh: 祝公明，處州麗水人。

translations.literal: Zhu Gongming was a man of Lishui in Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Gongming was from Lishui in Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 太原府盂縣主簿。

translations.literal: He was chief clerk of Yu County in Taiyuan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He served as chief clerk of Yu County in Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 靖康間，金人犯河東，令棄官去，公明攝縣事，率保甲入援，圍守逾年，城陷不屈。

translations.literal: In Jingkang the Jurchens invaded Hedong; he was ordered to leave office but took charge of the county, led the militia to aid, and besieged for more than a year; when the city fell he would not submit.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jurchens invaded Hedong in Jingkang he was told to flee but took the county in hand, led militia to its relief, and held out over a year; when the city fell he would not yield.

sentences.zh: 子陶，為唐州司戶，中原失守，陶亦死官所。

translations.literal: His son Tao was registrar of Tang Prefecture; when the central plains were lost Tao also died at his post.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tao was registrar of Tang; when the heartland fell Tao died at his post.

sentences.zh: 建炎中，贈公明承事郎。

translations.literal: In Jianyan he was posthumously made Gentleman for Continuing Service.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianyan he was posthumously made Gentleman for Continuing Service.

sentences.zh: 薛慶，起群盜，據高郵，兵數萬人，多驍雋敢鬥，能以少擊眾，附者日多。

translations.literal: Xue Qing rose from banditry, held Gaoyou with tens of thousands of fierce fighters who could strike many with few; followers grew daily.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Qing began as a bandit chief at Gaoyou with tens of thousands of bold fighters who could beat larger forces; men flocked to him.

sentences.zh: 張浚聞慶無所係屬，欲歸麾下，親往招之。

translations.literal: Zhang Jun heard Qing belonged to no one and wished him under his banner; he went in person to recruit him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun, hearing Qing owed allegiance to no one, went himself to win him.

sentences.zh: 慶感服，因使守高郵，尋遷拱衛大夫、福州觀察使、承州天長軍鎮撫使。

translations.literal: Qing was moved and submitted; he was set to hold Gaoyou, then made Grandee of the Palace Guard, Observer of Fuzhou, and pacifier of Tianchang Army in Cheng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Moved, Qing submitted; he held Gaoyou, then became Grandee of the Palace Guard, observer of Fuzhou, and pacifier of Tianchang in Cheng.

sentences.zh: 金人還自浙，屯天長、六合間，慶率眾劫之，得牛數百，悉賤估分畀民之力田者。

translations.literal: When the Jurchens returned from Zhe and camped between Tianchang and Liuhe, Qing raided them and took hundreds of oxen, selling them cheaply to farmers who had lost fields.
translations.idiomatic: As the Jurchens withdrew through Zhe and camped between Tianchang and Liuhe, Qing raided them, took hundreds of oxen, and sold them cheaply to ruined farmers.

sentences.zh: 金人欲自運河引舟北歸，而趙立在楚，慶在承，扼其衝不得進。

translations.literal: The Jurchens wished to bring boats north by the canal, but Zhao Li held Chu and Qing held Cheng, blocking their advance.
translations.idiomatic: They meant to use the canal northward, but Zhao Li at Chu and Qing at Cheng blocked the route.

sentences.zh: 金左監軍昌來見兀术，欲會兵攻楚州，真、揚鎮撫郭仲威聞之，約慶俱往迎敵。

translations.literal: The Jurchen Left Supervisor Chang came to see Wuzhu and wished to unite armies to attack Chuzhou; Guo Zhongwei of Zhen and Yang heard and arranged to meet Qing to oppose them.
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchen Left Supervisor Chang sought Wuzhu to strike Chuzhou; Guo Zhongwei of Zhen and Yang asked Qing to join him.

sentences.zh: 慶至揚州，仲威殊無行意，置酒高會。

translations.literal: Qing reached Yangzhou; Zhongwei had no mind to march and held a lofty feast.
translations.idiomatic: Qing reached Yangzhou, but Zhongwei would not march and only feasted.

sentences.zh: 慶怒曰：「此豈縱酒時耶？

translations.literal: Qing raged: “Is this a time for wine?
translations.idiomatic: Qing raged: “Is this a time for wine?

sentences.zh: 我為先鋒，汝當繼後。」

translations.literal: I go as vanguard—you follow after.”
translations.idiomatic: I will lead; you follow.”

sentences.zh: 上馬疾馳去，平旦出揚州西門，從騎不滿百，轉戰十餘里，亡騎三人，仲威迄不至。

translations.literal: He mounted and galloped off; at dawn he left Yangzhou’s west gate with fewer than a hundred followers, fought more than ten li, lost three horsemen, and Zhongwei never came.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn he rode out the west gate with under a hundred men, fought ten-odd li, lost three riders, and Zhongwei never came.

sentences.zh: 慶與其下奔揚州，仲威閉門拒之，慶倉皇墜馬，為金追騎所獲。

translations.literal: Qing and his men fled to Yangzhou; Zhongwei shut the gates. Qing fell in haste from his horse and was taken by Jurchen pursuers.
translations.idiomatic: Qing turned to Yangzhou; Zhongwei shut him out. He fell from his horse and Jurchen pursuers seized him.

sentences.zh: 馬識舊路還，軍中見之曰：「馬還，太尉其死乎。」

translations.literal: The horse knew the road and returned; the army said: “The horse is back—the Grand Marshal must be dead.”
translations.idiomatic: His horse found its way back; the troops said, “The horse returned—the Grand Marshal must be dead.”

sentences.zh: 金人殺慶，承州陷。

translations.literal: The Jurchens killed Qing and Cheng Prefecture fell.
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchens killed Qing, and Cheng fell.

sentences.zh: 訃聞，贈保寧軍承宣使，官其家十人，封其妻碩人。

translations.literal: On the report he was posthumously made Grandee of the Pacifying Army, ten in his family were given office, and his wife was ennobled as Lady.
translations.idiomatic: The court posthumously made him Grandee of the Pacifying Army, enrolled ten kin, and ennobled his wife.

sentences.zh: 孫暉，為泗州招信縣尉。

translations.literal: Sun Hui was sheriff of Zhaoxin County in Si Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hui was sheriff of Zhaoxin in Si Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 建炎三年正月，金人陷泗州，州守呂元、閻瑾焚淮橋遁。

translations.literal: In the first month of Jianyan 3 the Jurchens took Si; Prefect Lü Yuan and Yan Jin burned the Huai bridge and fled.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Jianyan 3 the Jurchens took Si; Prefect Lü Yuan and Yan Jin burned the Huai bridge and fled.

sentences.zh: 金人由招信將渡淮，暉將射士民兵禦之，沈其數舟。

translations.literal: Jurchens from Zhaoxin were about to cross the Huai; Hui led archers and militia to oppose them and sank several boats.
translations.idiomatic: Jurchens from Zhaoxin were crossing the Huai; Hui led archers and militia, sinking several boats.

sentences.zh: 會大霧蔽日，金人莫測其多寡，相持逾半日，以疑兵縻暉，自上流渡兵。

translations.literal: Heavy fog hid the sun; the Jurchens could not tell their numbers; they held half a day, then used a feint to pin Hui while crossing upstream.
translations.idiomatic: Fog blanketed the day; the Jurchens could not gauge his strength. After half a day they feinted at Hui and crossed upstream.

sentences.zh: 暉又戰且卻，城破，竟死於敕書樓。

translations.literal: Hui fought while retreating; the city fell and he died in the Imperial Writ Tower.
translations.idiomatic: Fighting as he withdrew, he died in the Imperial Writ Tower when the city fell.

sentences.zh: 李靚字彥和，吉州龍泉人。

translations.literal: Li Jing, style Yanhe, was a man of Longquan in Ji Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jing, style Yanhe, was from Longquan in Ji.

sentences.zh: 幼孤，母督之學，不肯卒業，母詰之，辭曰：「國家遭女真之變，寓縣雲擾，士當捐軀為國勘大憝，安能呫囁章句間，效淺丈夫哉？」

translations.literal: Orphaned young, his mother urged study; he refused, saying: “The state suffers the Jurchen disaster; the realm is in turmoil—a scholar should give his body to strike the great foe; how can he mutter over chapters like a petty man?”
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned, he refused his mother’s urging to study: “The realm suffers the Jurchen blow; a gentleman should die striking the foe, not mutter over chapters like a clerk.”

sentences.zh: 岳飛督師平虔寇，挺身從之，未行，奔母喪。

translations.literal: When Yue Fei marched to pacify the rebels of Qian, he went to join him but turned back for his mother’s mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He was about to join Yue Fei against the Qian rebels when his mother died and he withdrew.

sentences.zh: 服除，走淮南，以策幹都督張浚，浚奇之，使隸淮西總管孫暉戲下。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he went to Huainan and presented plans to Commissioner Zhang Jun, who was impressed and placed him under Sun Hui.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he went to Huainan, impressed Zhang Jun, and was placed under Sun Hui.

sentences.zh: 累功授承信郎。

translations.literal: For accumulated merit he was made Gentleman for Trusting the Court.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he was made Gentleman for Trusting the Court.

sentences.zh: 紹興十年，金遣其將翟將軍犯境，靚與部曲當其鋒，轉戰至西京天津橋南，俘翟將軍，乘勝逐北。

translations.literal: In Shaoxing 10 the Jurchen general Zhai invaded; Jing met his vanguard, fought to south of the Tianjin Bridge in the Western Capital, captured General Zhai, and pursued north.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaoxing 10 Jurchen General Zhai invaded; Jing met him, fought south of the Tianjin Bridge at the Western Capital, captured Zhai, and pursued.

sentences.zh: 會金兵大至，遂死之，年三十一。

translations.literal: Jurchen forces came in great numbers and he died—aged thirty-one.
translations.idiomatic: When Jurchen masses arrived he was killed—thirty-one years old.

sentences.zh: 楊照者，濠州將官也。

translations.literal: Yang Zhao was a garrison officer of Hao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zhao was an officer of Hao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 金人圍城急，照躍上角樓，刺賊之執黑旗者，洞腹抽腸而死。

translations.literal: As the Jurchens pressed the siege, Zhao leaped to the corner tower and stabbed the man holding the black banner, disemboweling him.
translations.idiomatic: When the siege grew desperate Zhao leaped to the tower, stabbed the black-banner bearer, and tore out his entrails.

sentences.zh: 照俄中流矢，卒。

translations.literal: Zhao soon took an arrow and died.
translations.idiomatic: He soon took an arrow and fell.

sentences.zh: 有統領丁元者，遇金人十八里洲，被圍，元大呼其徒，勉以毋得負國。

translations.literal: Commander Ding Yuan, at Eighteen-li Isle, was surrounded; Yuan cried to his men to never betray the state.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Ding Yuan, surrounded at Eighteen-li Isle, told his men never to betray the state.

sentences.zh: 一舟二百人皆鬥死。

translations.literal: All two hundred on one boat fought to the death.
translations.idiomatic: All two hundred on his boat fought to the death.

sentences.zh: 詔並贈承信郎，錄其後。

translations.literal: The throne posthumously made them Gentlemen for Trusting the Court and enrolled their descendants.
translations.idiomatic: The court posthumously made them Gentlemen for Trusting the Court and enrolled their kin.

sentences.zh: 宋昌祚，和州鈐轄也。

translations.literal: Song Changzuo was commander of He Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Song Changzuo was commander of He Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 建炎三年，兀术犯和州，州人推昌祚權領軍事，率眾堅守，金人圍之數匝。

translations.literal: In Jianyan 3 Wuzhu attacked He; the people made Changzuo provisional commander; he held firm while the Jurchens ringed the city.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianyan 3 Wuzhu attacked He; the people put Changzuo in command; he held while the Jurchens ringed the walls.

sentences.zh: 禁軍左指揮使鄭立亦拳勇忠憤，共激士卒，晝夜備禦不少怠。

translations.literal: Left commander Zheng Li was also brave and loyal; together they roused the troops to defend day and night without slack.
translations.idiomatic: Commander Zheng Li was equally fierce and loyal; together they kept the defense unceasing.

sentences.zh: 閱數日，軍士胡廣發弩中兀术左臂，兀术大怒，飛炮雨集，徑登弩發之地，城立破，金人入屠其城。

translations.literal: After several days soldier Hu Guang’s bolt struck Wuzhu’s left arm; Wuzhu raged, rained catapults, climbed where the bolts had flown, the wall fell, the Jurchens entered and slaughtered the city.
translations.idiomatic: After days Hu Guang’s bolt struck Wuzhu’s arm; enraged, Wuzhu battered the wall, stormed the breach, and massacred the city.

sentences.zh: 昌祚與權倅唐璟、曆陽令蹇譽、司戶徐兟、縣尉邵元通及立、廣皆死譙樓上，磔裂以徇。

translations.literal: Changzuo, acting vice-prefect Tang Jing, Liyang magistrate Jian Yu, registrar Xu Shen, sheriff Shao Yuantong, Li, and Guang all died on the watchtower, dismembered to warn others.
translations.idiomatic: Changzuo, Tang Jing, Jian Yu, Xu Shen, Shao Yuantong, Li, and Guang died on the watchtower, their bodies dismembered as a warning.

sentences.zh: 軍士多不降，潰圍西出，保麻湖水砦，推鄉豪為統領。

translations.literal: Many soldiers would not submit, broke out west, and held the Mazhu water fort, choosing a local leader as commander.
translations.idiomatic: Many soldiers refused surrender, broke west, and held the Mazhu water fort under a local chief.

sentences.zh: 聞於朝，遂以趙霖為和州鎮撫使，昌祚、璟、譽、兟、元通各贈官，錄其子弟。

translations.literal: The court made Zhao Lin pacifier of He; Changzuo, Jing, Yu, Shen, and Yuantong were each posthumously advanced and their sons enrolled.
translations.idiomatic: The court made Zhao Lin pacifier; the dead were posthumously honored and their sons enrolled.

sentences.zh: 李政，為雲騎第六指揮，在京東立戰功，補官授河北將官，冀州駐紮。

translations.literal: Li Zheng was of the Sixth Cloud Cavalry Command; he won merit in Jingdong and was made a Hebei officer stationed at Ji Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zheng of the Sixth Cloud Cavalry won merit in Jingdong and became a Hebei officer at Ji.

sentences.zh: 靖康二年，知州權邦彥以兵赴元帥府勤王，金兵來攻，政守禦有法，紀律嚴明，軍民皆不敢犯。

translations.literal: In Jingkang 2 Vice-Prefect Quan Bangyan marched to the marshal’s camp; the Jurchens attacked; Zheng defended with method and strict discipline so none dared offend.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingkang 2 Quan Bangyan marched to aid the court; when the Jurchens attacked, Zheng held Ji with discipline none dared break.

sentences.zh: 金屢攻城，政皆卻之。

translations.literal: The Jurchens attacked many times and he repelled them.
translations.idiomatic: They assaulted the walls repeatedly and he drove them back.

sentences.zh: 夜搗其砦，所得財物盡散士卒，無纖毫入私家。

translations.literal: By night he raided their camp and gave all spoils to the troops, not a thread to his own house.
translations.idiomatic: He raided their camp by night and gave every prize to the ranks, keeping nothing.

sentences.zh: 號令明，賞罰信，由是人皆用命。

translations.literal: Orders were clear and rewards sure, so all obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: Clear orders and sure rewards made every man obey.

sentences.zh: 俄攻城甚急，有登城者，火其門樓，與官兵相隔，政呼曰：「事急矣。

translations.literal: Soon the assault grew fierce; some climbed the wall and burned the gate tower, separating them from the troops. Zheng cried: “The crisis is upon us.
translations.idiomatic: When the assault grew fierce men scaled the wall and burned the gate tower. Zheng shouted: “The crisis is here!

sentences.zh: 有能躍火而過者，有重賞。」

translations.literal: Whoever can leap the fire shall have a great reward.”
translations.idiomatic: Whoever leaps the flames will be richly rewarded!”

sentences.zh: 於是有十數人皆以濕氈裹身，持仗躍火而過，大呼力戰，金人驚駭，有失仗者，遂敗走。

translations.literal: Then a dozen men wrapped wet felt about themselves, took weapons, leaped the fire, shouted and fought fiercely; the Jurchens were startled, some dropped weapons, and fled.
translations.idiomatic: A dozen wrapped themselves in wet felt, leaped the fire, and fought so fiercely the Jurchens fled in panic.

sentences.zh: 政大喜，皆厚賞之。

translations.literal: Zheng rejoiced and rewarded them richly.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng rejoiced and rewarded them handsomely.

sentences.zh: 未幾政死，城遂陷。

translations.literal: Before long Zheng died and the city fell.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Zheng died and the city fell.

sentences.zh: 權知州事單某者不降，自經死。

translations.literal: Acting prefect Shan would not submit and hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: Acting Prefect Shan refused surrender and hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 姜綬，處州麗水人。

translations.literal: Jiang Shou was a man of Lishui in Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Shou was from Lishui in Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 金人再犯京師，內外不相聞。

translations.literal: When the Jurchens again attacked the capital, inside and outside could not communicate.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jurchens again besieged the capital, court and provinces were cut off.

sentences.zh: 朝遷募忠勇士齎蠟書往南京總管司調兵赴援，綬以忠翊郎應募，乃刲股藏書，縋下南壁，為邏騎所獲，厲聲叱罵，遂被害。

translations.literal: The court sought brave men to carry wax letters to the Nanjing command to summon troops; Shou, as Gentleman for Assisting Loyalty, answered the call, cut his thigh to hide the letter, lowered himself from the south wall, was seized by border riders, and cursed them until he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: The court sought couriers; Shou cut his thigh to hide a wax letter, lowered himself from the wall, was taken, and cursed his captors until they killed him.

sentences.zh: 建炎中，州上其事，官其子特立承信郎。

translations.literal: In Jianyan the prefecture reported it and his son Teli was made Gentleman for Trusting the Court.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianyan his son Teli was made Gentleman for Trusting the Court.

sentences.zh: 劉宣，為秦鳳路兵馬都監。

translations.literal: Liu Xuan was overall commander of Qin-Feng troops.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xuan was overall commander of Qin-Feng forces.

sentences.zh: 金人入關、陝，宣遣蠟書密與吳玠相結，且率金將任拱等以所部歸朝。

translations.literal: When the Jurchens entered the passes and Shaanxi, Xuan sent a wax letter secretly to Wu Jie and led the Jurchen officer Ren Gong and his command to defect.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jurchens entered the passes he sent a wax letter to Wu Jie and planned to bring Ren Gong’s command over.

sentences.zh: 約日已定，有告之者，金人取宣縷擘之，其家屬配曹州。

translations.literal: The day was fixed; someone informed; the Jurchens took Xuan and tore him apart; his family was sent to Cao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The day was set but he was betrayed; the Jurchens dismembered him and sent his family to Cao.

sentences.zh: 屈堅，為右武大夫、忠州防禦使。

translations.literal: Qu Jian was Grandee of the Right Guard and defender of Zhong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Jian was Grandee of the Right Guard and defender of Zhong.

sentences.zh: 建炎二年，金人圍陝府，堅引所部救之。

translations.literal: In Jianyan 2 the Jurchens besieged Shanfu; Jian led his troops to relieve it.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianyan 2 he led troops to relieve the siege of Shanfu.

sentences.zh: 圍解，金人執堅，堅曰：「始吾所以來，為解圍也。

translations.literal: The siege lifted; the Jurchens seized Jian. Jian said: “I came only to lift the siege.
translations.idiomatic: When the siege lifted they seized him. He said: “I came only to break the siege.

sentences.zh: 城苟全，吾死何憾。」

translations.literal: If the city is safe, what regret have I in death?”
translations.idiomatic: If the city stands, I do not regret death.”

sentences.zh: 叱金人使速殺之。

translations.literal: He berated the Jurchens to kill him quickly.
translations.idiomatic: He cursed them to kill him at once.

sentences.zh: 後贈三官，錄其家五人。

translations.literal: Later he was posthumously advanced three ranks and five in his family were enrolled.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was advanced three ranks posthumously and five kin enrolled.

sentences.zh: 王琦，為弓門砦巡檢。

translations.literal: Wang Qi was inspector of Gongmen Stockade.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qi was inspector of Gongmen Stockade.

sentences.zh: 建炎四年，金人還自熙河，琦禦之。

translations.literal: In Jianyan 4 the Jurchens returned from Xihe; Qi opposed them.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianyan 4 the Jurchens withdrew from Xihe and Qi opposed them.

sentences.zh: 金人立招降旗榜，改年號阜昌，眾皆拜，琦獨不屈。

translations.literal: The Jurchens raised a surrender banner and changed the era to Fuchang; all bowed except Qi.
translations.idiomatic: They raised a surrender banner and changed the era name; all bowed but Qi.

sentences.zh: 金人執而殺之。

translations.literal: The Jurchens seized and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchens seized him and killed him.

sentences.zh: 韋永壽者，紹興三十二年，以統製官與金人戰和州，子承節郎世堅救之，同死。

translations.literal: Wei Yongshou—in Shaoxing 32, as overall controller he fought the Jurchens at He; his son Shijian, Instructor of the Court, tried to save him and both died.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaoxing 32 Wei Yongshou fought the Jurchens at He; his son Shijian tried to save him and both fell.

sentences.zh: 張浚以言，贈中衛大夫、融州觀察使，世堅贈三官。

translations.literal: Zhang Jun reported it; Yongshou was posthumously made Grandee of the Central Guard and Observer of Rong, and Shijian three ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun reported it; Yongshou was posthumously made observer of Rong, Shijian advanced three ranks.

sentences.zh: 鄭覃，字季厚，明州人。

translations.literal: Zheng Tan, style Jihou, was a man of Ming Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Tan, style Jihou, was from Ming.

sentences.zh: 靖康二年貢於鄉。

translations.literal: In Jingkang 2 he was presented at the prefectural examination.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingkang 2 he presented himself at the prefectural examination.

sentences.zh: 建炎四年春，金人陷明州，縱兵大掠，覃挈族辟難山谷間。

translations.literal: In spring of Jianyan 4 the Jurchens took Ming and plundered; Tan led his clan to refuge in the hills.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of Jianyan 4 the Jurchens took Ming and plundered; Tan led his clan into the hills.

sentences.zh: 金人追及，與兄章俱被執，脅以刃，曰：「予吾金，即貰死。」

translations.literal: The Jurchens overtook him; he and his elder brother Zhang were seized; blades at their throats they said: “Give us gold and we spare your lives.”
translations.idiomatic: Overtaken, he and his brother Zhang were seized; blades at their throats: “Give gold and live.”

sentences.zh: 覃號泣指所瘞黃金釵遺之，遂見釋。

translations.literal: Tan wept and pointed to buried gold hairpins; they were released.
translations.idiomatic: Tan wept, pointed to buried gold hairpins, and was released.

sentences.zh: 而金兵相屬，覃拿小舟與其妻董同載去，顧謂章曰：「萬一不得脫，覃豈北面事異國者，兄勉主祭祀。」

translations.literal: Jurchen troops came in succession; Tan took a small boat with his wife Dong and said to Zhang: “If we cannot escape, Tan will not bow to a foreign state—brother, keep the sacrifices.”
translations.idiomatic: More troops came; Tan fled by boat with his wife Dong and told Zhang: “If we cannot escape I will not serve the enemy—keep the rites.”

sentences.zh: 復為兵所劫去，迫使之降，覃厲辭罵不屈，躍入水中。

translations.literal: Again seized and forced to submit, Tan cursed fiercely and would not yield, and leaped into the water.
translations.idiomatic: Seized again and ordered to submit, he cursed and leaped into the river.

sentences.zh: 董哭曰：「夫亡矣，與其受辱以生，不如死。」

translations.literal: Dong wept: “My husband is gone; better die than live in shame.”
translations.idiomatic: Dong cried: “My husband is gone—I will not live in shame.”

sentences.zh: 亦自沈。

translations.literal: She too drowned herself.
translations.idiomatic: She drowned herself.

sentences.zh: 覃死後，孫、曾多舉進士，而清之最顯。

translations.literal: After Tan’s death many grandsons and great-grandsons passed the jinshi; Qing was most prominent.
translations.idiomatic: After his death many descendants became jinshi; Qing was most eminent.

sentences.zh: 覃累贈太師、秦國公，董秦國夫人。

translations.literal: Tan was repeatedly posthumously made Grand Preceptor and Duke of Qin; Dong was made Lady of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Tan was posthumously made Grand Preceptor and Duke of Qin; Dong was Lady of Qin.

sentences.zh: 姚興，相州人。

translations.literal: Yao Xing was a man of Xiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing was from Xiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 靖康中，以州校用。

translations.literal: In Jingkang he was used as a garrison soldier.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingkang he served as a garrison soldier.

sentences.zh: 劫殺金人有功，借補承信郎。

translations.literal: For killing Jurchens in raids he was provisionally made Gentleman for Trusting the Court.
translations.idiomatic: For killing Jurchens in raids he was made Gentleman for Trusting the Court.

sentences.zh: 建炎初，張琪聚兵歸東京留守宗澤，興往從之，又從琪依劉洪道於池州。

translations.literal: At the start of Jianyan Zhang Qi gathered troops and joined Tokyo custodian Zong Ze; Xing followed Qi, then followed Qi to Liu Hongdao at Chi.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jianyan Zhang Qi joined Zong Ze; Xing followed Qi, then Liu Hongdao at Chi.

sentences.zh: 紹興元年，琪叛，掠饒州，呂頤浩招降之。

translations.literal: In Shaoxing 1 Qi rebelled and plundered Raozhou; Lü Yiyao induced him to submit.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaoxing 1 Qi rebelled at Raozhou; Lü Yiyao brought him in.

sentences.zh: 琪既聽命而中變，執總管巨師古將殺之，興密諭所部，挾師古同其妻遊騎而馳，夜歸頤浩。

translations.literal: Qi agreed but turned again, seized overall commander Ju Shigu to kill him; Xing secretly roused his men, took Shigu and his wife on a night ride, and returned to Yiyao.
translations.idiomatic: Qi turned traitor and seized Ju Shigu; Xing secretly rescued Shigu and fled to Yiyao by night.

sentences.zh: 頤浩義之，請於朝，授武義郎，隸張俊軍中。

translations.literal: Yiyao praised him and asked the court to make him Gentleman for Martial Righteousness under Zhang Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Yiyao praised him; the court made him Gentleman for Martial Righteousness under Zhang Jun.

sentences.zh: 復從劉錡守順昌，復宿、亳，下城父、永城、臨渙、蘄縣朱家村，遷武略大夫。

translations.literal: He followed Liu Qi at Shunchang, recovered Su and Bo, took Chengfu, Yongcheng, Linhuan, and Qixian Zhujia village, and was made Grandee for Martial Strategy.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Liu Qi at Shunchang, recovered cities along the Huai, and rose to Grandee for Martial Strategy.

sentences.zh: 戰淮壖有功，授右武大夫，累遷建康府駐紮御前破敵軍統製，充荊湖南路兵馬副都監。

translations.literal: For merit on the Huai frontier he was made Grandee of the Right Guard, overall controller of the Front-Army Breakers at Jiankang, and vice-commander of Jinghu South.
translations.idiomatic: For Huai campaigns he became controller at Jiankang and vice-commander of Jinghu South.

sentences.zh: 紹興三十一年，金人渝盟，興隸都統王權麾下，遇金兵五百騎於廬州之定林，與戰卻之，生得女直鶻殺虎。

translations.literal: In Shaoxing 31 the Jurchens broke the treaty; Xing served under Overall Commander Wang Quan, met five hundred Jurchen horsemen at Dinglin in Luzhou, drove them back, and captured the Jurchen Husaha alive.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaoxing 31, under Wang Quan, he met five hundred Jurchens at Dinglin, routed them, and captured Husaha.

sentences.zh: 初，金主亮在壽春，江、淮製置使劉錡命權將兵迎敵，權怯懦不進，錡督戰益急，權不得已守廬州。

translations.literal: Earlier Jurchen ruler Liang was at Shouchun; Commissioner Liu Qi ordered Quan to advance; Quan was timid and would not march until Qi pressed him to hold Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang was at Shouchun, Liu Qi ordered Quan forward; cowardly Quan only held Luzhou under pressure.

sentences.zh: 及金兵渡淮，權遣興拒之，而退保和州。

translations.literal: When the Jurchens crossed the Huai, Quan sent Xing to oppose them but withdrew to protect He.
translations.idiomatic: When they crossed the Huai, Quan sent Xing forward but himself withdrew to He.

sentences.zh: 興與金人遇於尉子橋，金人以鐵騎進，興麾兵力戰，手殺數百人。

translations.literal: Xing met them at Weizi Bridge; the Jurchens advanced with iron cavalry; Xing waved his troops to fight and personally killed hundreds.
translations.idiomatic: At Weizi Bridge iron cavalry charged; Xing fought hand to hand and killed hundreds.

sentences.zh: 權奔仙宗山，嚴兵自衛，興告急不應，統領戴皋帥馬軍引避。

translations.literal: Quan fled to Xianzong Mountain and barred himself in; Xing begged aid in vain; Commander Dai Gao led the horse troops away.
translations.idiomatic: Quan fled to Xianzong Mountain; Xing’s pleas went unanswered; Dai Gao withdrew the cavalry.

sentences.zh: 初，李二者，嘗有私恩於權，因得出入軍中，往來兩界貿易，間竊權旗幟遺金人。

translations.literal: Earlier Li Er had owed Quan a private favor and traded between the lines, sometimes giving Quan’s banners to the Jurchens.
translations.idiomatic: Li Er, who had favored Quan, traded across the lines and once gave Jurchens Quan’s banners.

sentences.zh: 至是，金人立權旗幟以誤興，興往奔之，父子俱死焉。

translations.literal: Now the Jurchens raised Quan’s banners to deceive Xing; he rushed toward them and father and son both died.
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchens raised Quan’s banners; Xing charged and he and his son both fell.

sentences.zh: 事聞，詔贈容州觀察使，又特官其後三人，即其砦立廟。

translations.literal: Reported, he was posthumously made Observer of Rong; three more in his family were given office and a temple was raised at his fort.
translations.idiomatic: The court posthumously made him observer of Rong, enrolled three kin, and built a temple at his fort.

sentences.zh: 既復淮西，又立廟戰所，賜額旌忠。

translations.literal: When the west of the Huai was recovered, another temple was built at the battlefield with the name “Exalting Loyalty.”
translations.idiomatic: When the Huai west was recovered, another temple was built on the field, named Exalting Loyalty.

sentences.zh: 開禧元年，戶部侍郎趙善堅言：「近守邊藩，詢訪故老，姚興以四百騎當金人十數萬，自辰至午，戰數十合，援兵不至，竟死於敵。

translations.literal: In Kaixi 1 Vice Minister Zhao Shanjian said: "Having lately guarded a border post, I asked old men—Yao Xing with four hundred horsemen faced tens of thousands of Jurchens from the chen hour to noon, fought dozens of clashes, and with no relief finally died before the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaixi 1 Zhao Shanjian said: "Having lately guarded a border post, I asked old men—Yao Xing with four hundred horsemen faced tens of thousands of Jurchens from the chen hour to noon, fought dozens of clashes, and with no relief finally died before the enemy.

sentences.zh: 金人相謂曰：『有如姚興者十輩，吾屬敢前乎？』

translations.literal: The Jurchens said to one another, 'If there were ten men like Yao Xing, would any of us dare advance?'
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchens said, 'If there were ten men like Yao Xing, would any of us dare advance?'

sentences.zh: 興忠勇如此，宜超加爵諡。」

translations.literal: Xing was so loyal and brave; he should receive exalted posthumous rank.”
translations.idiomatic: So loyal and brave—he should receive exalted honors.”

sentences.zh: 於是賜諡忠毅。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was given the posthumous name Zhongyi.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous name Zhongyi.

sentences.zh: 張玘字伯玉。

translations.literal: Zhang Qi, style Boyu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Qi, style Boyu.

sentences.zh: 世居河南澠池。

translations.literal: His family had long lived in Mianchi, Henan.
translations.idiomatic: His family lived in Mianchi, Henan.

sentences.zh: 建炎中，以家財募兵討金人，從者數千人。

translations.literal: In Jianyan he raised troops at his own expense against the Jurchens; thousands followed.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianyan he raised troops at his own expense; thousands followed.

sentences.zh: 時翟興製置京西，玘以眾屬焉。

translations.literal: Zhai Xing was commissioner of Jingxi; Qi placed himself under him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Xing commanded Jingxi; Qi joined him.

sentences.zh: 金兵長驅渡河，玘禦之白浪口，金人不得渡。

translations.literal: The Jurchens drove deep across the river; Qi blocked them at Bailang Ford and they could not cross.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jurchens drove deep, Qi held Bailang Ford and they could not cross.

sentences.zh: 積功補武翼大夫、成州刺史。

translations.literal: For merit he was made Grandee for Martial Wings and prefect of Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he was made Grandee for Martial Wings and prefect of Cheng.

sentences.zh: 董先為製置司前軍統製，玘佐之，每戰，冒矢石為諸軍先。

translations.literal: Dong Xian commanded the forward army of the commission; Qi assisted him and in every battle led the van through arrow and stone.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Xian led the forward army; Qi always charged first through fire.

sentences.zh: 紹興元年，金將高瓊率眾取商州。

translations.literal: In Shaoxing 1 Jurchen general Gao Qiong led troops to take Shang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaoxing 1 the Jurchen general Gao Qiong marched on Shang.

sentences.zh: 董先禦之，玘乘銳奔擊，從騎不能屬，單馬至四皓廟，金兵數百騎至，玘瞋目大呼，挺刃突擊，金兵披靡莫敢向。

translations.literal: Dong Xian resisted; Qi charged with picked men, his escort could not keep up, and alone he reached the Temple of the Four Hoary Ones; hundreds of Jurchen horsemen came; Qi glared, shouted, and thrust forward; the Jurchens scattered and dared not face him.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Xian held them off; Qi charged ahead alone to the Temple of the Four Hoary Ones, glared and hacked through hundreds of Jurchen horsemen who dared not face him.

sentences.zh: 是日，九戰九捷，追至試劍關，爭門蹂踐死者百人。

translations.literal: That day he fought nine battles and won nine; pursuing to Trial Sword Pass, a hundred died trampled at the gate.
translations.idiomatic: That day he won nine battles in a row; at Trial Sword Pass a hundred died in the crush at the gate.

sentences.zh: 明年春，偕先繇藍田渡渭，規取長安。

translations.literal: The next spring, with Xian he crossed the Wei from Lantian planning to take Chang’an.
translations.idiomatic: The next spring he crossed the Wei from Lantian with Xian to retake Chang’an.

sentences.zh: 時偽齊經略使李諤屯渭北，與金將折合孛堇相為聲勢。

translations.literal: The false Qi commissioner Li E camped north of the Wei and coordinated with Jurchen general Zhehe Bojin.
translations.idiomatic: False Qi commissioner Li E camped north of the Wei in concert with the Jurchen general Zhehe Bojin.

sentences.zh: 玘陳兵華嚴川，俄白氣貫日，吏士歡奮，戰於興平、咸陽、渭河、石鱉谷。

translations.literal: Qi arrayed troops on Huayan Stream; soon a white vapor pierced the sun; officers and soldiers rejoiced and fought at Xingping, Xianyang, the Wei, and Stone Turtle Valley.
translations.idiomatic: Qi drew up on Huayan Stream; when a white vapor pierced the sun his men fought at Xingping, Xianyang, the Wei, and Stone Turtle Valley.

sentences.zh: 時劉豫據京師，先軍乏食，偽降豫，不挈家，玘事其夫人如舊。

translations.literal: Liu Yu held the capital; Xian’s army lacked food and feigned submission to Yu without bringing families; Qi served Xian’s wife as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yu held the capital, Xian feigned submission; Qi still served Xian’s wife faithfully.

sentences.zh: 豫使人迎其妻，先密書報玘勿遣，且述必還意。

translations.literal: Yu sent for Xian’s wife; Xian secretly wrote Qi not to send her and vowed to return.
translations.idiomatic: Yu demanded Xian’s wife; Xian secretly told Qi to refuse and vowed to return.

sentences.zh: 王倚攝虢州，從偽意堅，玘患之。

translations.literal: Wang Yi held Guo Prefecture and favored the pretender; Qi was troubled.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yi of Guo favored the pretender; Qi was troubled.

sentences.zh: 會別將董震自商州來，倚喜曰：「震與我善，今以兵來，天讚我也。」

translations.literal: Commander Dong Zhen came from Shang; Yi rejoiced: “Zhen is my friend—his troops are heaven’s blessing.”
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhen came from Shang; Yi said: “Zhen is my friend—his arrival is heaven’s aid.”

sentences.zh: 乃與震謀害玘。

translations.literal: He plotted with Zhen to kill Qi.
translations.idiomatic: He plotted with Zhen to kill Qi.

sentences.zh: 震陽許而陰以告。

translations.literal: Zhen agreed openly but secretly informed Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen agreed openly but secretly warned Qi.

sentences.zh: 翼日，倚詣玘議事，玘叱下，責以大義，並推官祁宗儒斬之。

translations.literal: Next day Yi came to Qi’s council; Qi had him seized, rebuked him for treason, and with aide Qi Zongru beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Yi came to council; Qi seized him, rebuked him, and with Qi Zongru beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 先是，豫遣人持詔撫諭，以玘為商虢順州路兵馬都監、同統製軍馬，玘囚其使，至是並戮之。

translations.literal: Earlier Yu had sent envoys with edicts making Qi commander of Shang-Guo-Shun; Qi imprisoned the envoys; now he executed them too.
translations.idiomatic: Yu’s envoys had offered Qi command; he had imprisoned them and now executed them as well.

sentences.zh: 於是偽齊河南安撫孟邦雄、總管樊彥直據洛陽，兵直抵長水。

translations.literal: Then the false Qi’s Henan pacifier Meng Bangxiong and overall commander Fan Yanzhi held Luoyang and marched to Changshui.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Bangxiong and Fan Yanzhi of the false Qi marched from Luoyang to Changshui.

sentences.zh: 玘遣將陳俊守白馬山，謝皋守船板山，梁進守錦屏山，盡匿精銳。

translations.literal: Qi sent Chen Jun to hold White Horse Mountain, Xie Gao Shipboard Mountain, and Liang Jin Brocade Screen Mountain, hiding picked troops.
translations.idiomatic: Qi hid picked troops on White Horse, Shipboard, and Brocade Screen mountains.

sentences.zh: 金兵深入，玘戰東關，三砦響應，金兵潰。

translations.literal: The Jurchens advanced deep; Qi fought at East Pass; the three forts answered and the Jurchens broke.
translations.idiomatic: When Jurchens advanced, Qi fought at East Pass; the three forts answered and routed them.

sentences.zh: 玘率精騎三千，一日夜馳三百里，黎明抵河南，邦雄就擒，彥直遁去。

translations.literal: Qi led three thousand elite horsemen three hundred li in one day and night, reaching Henan at dawn; Bangxiong was taken and Yanzhi fled.
translations.idiomatic: Qi rode three thousand elite three hundred li in a day, took Bangxiong at dawn, and Yanzhi fled.

sentences.zh: 便宜升霸州防禦使。

translations.literal: He was provisionally made Defender of Ba Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Defender of Ba Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 三年春，先自偽齊歸，玘還兵柄，退就位，時人義之。

translations.literal: In spring of year three Xian returned from the false Qi; Qi restored the command and stepped back—men praised his righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: When Xian returned from the false Qi, Qi yielded command—men praised his honor.

sentences.zh: 初，翟興既死，朝廷命其子琮襲，至是琮言於朝，真授玘武翼大夫、果州團練使、河南府孟汝唐州馬步軍副總管。

translations.literal: When Zhai Xing died the court ordered his son Cong to succeed; Cong asked the court to confirm Qi as Grandee for Martial Wings, regimental commander of Guo, and vice-overall commander of Henan horse and foot.
translations.idiomatic: Cong asked the court to confirm Qi as commander of Henan forces.

sentences.zh: 擊金將閻銳於唐、鄧間，先登殺獲千餘人。

translations.literal: He struck the Jurchen Yan Rui between Tang and Deng, took the lead, and killed or captured over a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He struck Yan Rui between Tang and Deng at the fore and killed or captured a thousand.

sentences.zh: 未幾，詔先一行並聽神武后軍統製。

translations.literal: Soon the court ordered Xian’s whole line under the Rear Divine Martial Army.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Xian’s command was placed under the Rear Divine Martial Army.

sentences.zh: 玘從岳飛復京西六州，平湖賊鍾子義等，累功進拱衛大夫。

translations.literal: Qi followed Yue Fei to recover six prefectures of Jingxi and pacified bandit Zhong Ziyi, advancing to Grandee of the Palace Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Qi followed Yue Fei to recover Jingxi and rose to Grandee of the Palace Guard.

sentences.zh: 入侍衛，始以誅王倚事聞，敕付史館，賜褒詔，進親衛大夫。

translations.literal: Entering the guard, the killing of Wang Yi was reported; the Historiographical Office recorded it and an imperial commendation advanced him to Grandee of the Imperial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Entering the guard, his execution of Wang Yi won imperial praise and promotion.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，領御營宿衛前軍都統，屯泗州。

translations.literal: In year 32 he commanded the forward army of the Imperial Guard encampment and was stationed at Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In year 32 he commanded the Imperial Guard forward army at Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 時金人攻海州急，詔玘會鎮江都統制張子蓋赴之。

translations.literal: The Jurchens were pressing Haizhou hard; Qi was ordered to join Jiangdu overall commander Zhang Zigai in its relief.
translations.idiomatic: When Haizhou was hard pressed, Qi was ordered to join Zhang Zigai in its relief.

sentences.zh: 賊環城數十匝，矢石如雨，玘戰於州北三里，麾精騎衝其陣，手殺數十人，殲其長，殺獲萬計，海州圍解。

translations.literal: The enemy ringed the city dozens of times; arrows and stones fell like rain; Qi fought three li north of the prefecture, led elite cavalry against their line, personally killed dozens, destroyed their leader, and killed and captured by the tens of thousands; the siege of Haizhou was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy ringed the city; Qi fought three li north, led a cavalry charge, killed dozens with his own hand, slew their leader, and lifted the siege.

sentences.zh: 玘中流矢卒，子蓋上其功，特贈正任觀察使，官其後九人，廟號忠勇。

translations.literal: Qi was struck by an arrow and died; Zigai reported his merit; he was specially posthumously made regular Observer and nine descendants were given office; his temple name was Loyal and Brave.
translations.idiomatic: Qi died of an arrow wound; Zigai reported his merit; he was posthumously made Observer, nine kinsmen were enrolled, and his temple was named Loyal and Brave.

sentences.zh: 孝宗即位，又命祠於戰所，贈清遠軍承宣使。

translations.literal: When Xiaozong took the throne he again ordered sacrifice at the battlefield and posthumously made him Military Commissioner of Qingyuan Army.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozong ordered sacrifice at the battlefield and posthumously made him Military Commissioner of Qingyuan Army.

sentences.zh: 子世雄，歿於符離之戰，贈武節大夫。

translations.literal: His son Shixiong died at the battle of Fuli; he was posthumously made Grandee for Martial Discipline.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shixiong died at Fuli and was posthumously made Grandee for Martial Discipline.

sentences.zh: 陳亨祖者，淮寧大豪也。

translations.literal: Chen Hengzu was a great magnate of Huaining.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Hengzu was a great magnate of Huaining.

sentences.zh: 紹興末，官軍已復蔡州，亨祖遂領民兵據淮寧，執金知州完顏耶魯，以其城來歸。

translations.literal: Late in Shaoxing the army recovered Cai; Hengzu led militia to hold Huaining, seized Jurchen prefect Wanyan Yelu, and submitted the city.
translations.idiomatic: When Cai was recovered he held Huaining, seized the Jurchen prefect, and submitted.

sentences.zh: 命為武翼大夫、忠州刺史、知淮寧府。

translations.literal: He was made Grandee for Martial Wings, Prefect of Loyalty, and intendant of Huaining.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Grandee for Martial Wings and prefect of Huaining.

sentences.zh: 金兵攻城，亨祖力戰死之，舉家五十餘人皆死。

translations.literal: Jurchens besieged the city; Hengzu fought to the death; more than fifty of his household died.
translations.idiomatic: When Jurchens besieged Huaining he fought to the death; over fifty of his kin fell.

sentences.zh: 贈容州觀察使，立廟光州，賜額閔忠。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Observer of Rong; a temple was built at Guang with the name Pitying Loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously observer of Rong; a temple at Guang was named Pitying Loyalty.

sentences.zh: 王拱，建康府前軍統制。

translations.literal: Wang Gong was overall controller of the former army at Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gong was overall controller of Jiankang’s former army.

sentences.zh: 從都統邵宏淵收復虹縣，進取宿州，屢立奇功。

translations.literal: Following Overall Commander Shao Hongyuan he recovered Hong County and advanced on Suzhou with repeated feats.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Shao Hongyuan to recover Hong and advance on Suzhou with many feats.

sentences.zh: 隆興元年五月，與金人接戰，深入營中，自辰至申，力戰死。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of Longxing 1 he met the Jurchens, fought deep in their camp from dawn to afternoon, and died fighting.
translations.idiomatic: In Longxing 1 he fought in the Jurchen camp from dawn to afternoon and died.

sentences.zh: 詔贈正任觀察使，官其家八人。

translations.literal: The throne posthumously made him Regular Observer and enrolled eight of his family.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Regular Observer and eight kin enrolled.

sentences.zh: 許奏異姓，賜銀三百兩，即其砦立廟，賜額忠節。

translations.literal: He was allowed to recommend a non-kin heir, given three hundred taels of silver, and a temple at his fort named Loyal Fidelity.
translations.idiomatic: He could name an heir, received silver, and a temple named Loyal Fidelity.

sentences.zh: 是役也，中亮大夫朱贇亦死之，贈承宣使。

translations.literal: In that battle Grandee Zhu Yun also died and was posthumously made Grandee for Imperial Trust.
translations.idiomatic: Grandee Zhu Yun also died and was posthumously advanced.

sentences.zh: 劉泰，樞密院忠義前軍正將也。

translations.literal: Liu Tai was a front-army captain of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Tai was a front-army captain of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 慷慨好義，以私財募兵三百，糧儲器械一切不資於官。

translations.literal: Generous and righteous, he raised three hundred men at private expense without state grain or arms.
translations.idiomatic: He raised three hundred men at his own expense, taking nothing from the state.

sentences.zh: 金人犯壽春，泰率所部赴援，轉戰累日，金人引去，泰身被數十創，一夕死。

translations.literal: When the Jurchens attacked Shouchun, Tai led his men to aid, fought many days until they withdrew; Tai took dozens of wounds and died overnight.
translations.idiomatic: At Shouchun he fought many days, took dozens of wounds, and died overnight.

sentences.zh: 詔贈武翼郎，官其家三人。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Grandee for Martial Wings and three in his family were given office.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grandee for Martial Wings; three kin enrolled.

sentences.zh: 孫逢，眉山人。

translations.literal: Sun Feng was a man of Meizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Feng was from Meizhou.

sentences.zh: 大觀四年進士，累官至太學博士。

translations.literal: A jinshi in Daguan 4, he rose to Erudite of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: A Daguan 4 jinshi, he became Erudite of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 張邦昌僭立，有司趣百僚入賀，逢獨堅臥不起。

translations.literal: When Zhang Bangchang usurped, the offices hurried the hundred officials to congratulate; Feng alone would not rise.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Bangchang usurped, officials rushed to congratulate; Feng alone would not rise.

sentences.zh: 夜既半，同僚強起之，不從，至垂泣與之訣。

translations.literal: Past midnight colleagues forced him; he refused, wept and bade them farewell.
translations.idiomatic: Past midnight colleagues forced him; he wept and refused.

sentences.zh: 時祠部員外郎喻汝礪聞變，捫其膝曰：「不能為賊臣屈。」

translations.literal: Libationer Yu Rulü heard and smote his knee: “I cannot bow to a rebel minister.”
translations.idiomatic: Yu Rulü said: “I cannot bow to a rebel minister” and left office.

sentences.zh: 遂掛冠去。

translations.literal: He hung up his cap and went.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned.

sentences.zh: 事畢，有司舉不至者，欲以逢與汝礪復於金人，邦昌以畢至告，乃免。

translations.literal: Afterward the offices listed absentees to hand back to the Jurchens; Bangchang said all had come and Feng and Rulü were spared.
translations.idiomatic: Absentees were to be handed to the Jurchens; Bangchang lied that all had come and spared them.

sentences.zh: 逢聞之曰：「是必將肆赦遷官以重汙我，我其可俟！」

translations.literal: Feng heard and said: “They will surely pardon and promote to deepen the stain—I cannot wait!”
translations.idiomatic: Feng said: “They will pardon and promote to deepen our shame—I cannot wait!”

sentences.zh: 遂發疾而卒。

translations.literal: He fell ill and died.
translations.idiomatic: He fell ill and died.

sentences.zh: 李熙靖，晉陵人。

translations.literal: Li Xijing was a man of Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xijing was from Jinling.

sentences.zh: 提舉醴泉觀。

translations.literal: He was superintendent of the Liquan Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: He superintended the Liquan Abbey.

sentences.zh: 邦昌使直學士院，熙靖固拒，因憂憤不食，疾且篤，謂友人曰：「百官何日再朝天乎？」

translations.literal: Bangchang made him of the Academy; Xijing firmly refused, grieved and would not eat; gravely ill he said to friends: “When will the hundred officials face the Son of Heaven again?”
translations.idiomatic: Bangchang ordered him into the Academy; he firmly refused, would not eat from grief, and when gravely ill asked friends: "When will the hundred officials again face the Son of Heaven?"

sentences.zh: 泣數行下。

translations.literal: Tears ran in streams.
translations.idiomatic: Tears ran down his face.

sentences.zh: 邦昌又命禮部侍郎譚世績權直學士院，世績亦稱疾堅臥不起。

translations.literal: Bangchang also ordered Vice Minister of Rites Tan Shiji to act as academician; Shiji too pleaded illness and would not rise.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Shiji too pleaded illness and would not serve.

sentences.zh: 熙靖尋卒。

translations.literal: Xijing soon died.
translations.idiomatic: Xijing soon died.

sentences.zh: 後並贈延康殿學士。

translations.literal: Later both were posthumously made Academicians of the Hall of Extended Glory.
translations.idiomatic: Later both were posthumously made Academicians of Extended Glory.
