sentences.zh: 趙俊字德進，南京宋城人。

translations.literal: Zhao Jun, style Dejin, was a man of Songcheng in Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Jun, style Dejin, was from Songcheng.

sentences.zh: 紹聖四年進士，官至朝奉郎。

translations.literal: A jinshi in Shaosheng 4, he rose to Gentleman for Court Service.
translations.idiomatic: A Shaosheng 4 jinshi, he rose to Gentleman for Court Service.

sentences.zh: 隱居杜門，雖鄉里不妄交。

translations.literal: He lived in seclusion behind closed doors and would not mingle even with neighbors.
translations.idiomatic: He lived secluded and would not mingle even with neighbors.

sentences.zh: 劉安世無恙時居河南，暇則獨一過之。

translations.literal: When Liu Anshi was well at Henan, Jun alone visited him now and then.
translations.idiomatic: Only Liu Anshi at Henan occasionally visited him.

sentences.zh: 徐處仁與俊厚善，及為丞相，鄉人多見用，俊未嘗往求，處仁亦忘之，獨不得官。

translations.literal: Xu Churen was close to Jun; when he became chancellor many townsfolk were employed but Jun never sought him—Churen forgot him and he alone received no office.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu Churen became chancellor he employed many townsfolk but never Jun, who sought nothing.

sentences.zh: 建炎末，士大夫皆避地，俊獨不肯，曰：「但固吾所守爾，死生命也，避將安之？」

translations.literal: At the end of Jianyan gentry fled; Jun alone would not, saying: “I need only hold to what I guard—life and death are fate; where would flight take me?”
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Jianyan all fled; Jun said: “I hold to my post—life and death are fate; where would I flee?”

sentences.zh: 衣冠奔踣於道者相繼，俊晏然不動。

translations.literal: Officials in robes fell on the road one after another; Jun was unmoved.
translations.idiomatic: Officials fell on the road; Jun was unmoved.

sentences.zh: 劉豫以俊為虞部員外郎，辭疾不受，以告畀其家，卒卻之，如是再三，豫亦不復強。

translations.literal: Liu Yu made him Vice Director of the Ministry of Works; he pleaded illness and refused; Yu reported it and gave to his family; he still refused thrice and Yu did not press him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu offered him office; he refused thrice and Yu did not force him.

sentences.zh: 凡家書文字，一不用豫僭號，但書甲子。

translations.literal: In all family letters he never used Yu’s reign title but only wrote the sexagenary year.
translations.idiomatic: In letters he never used Yu’s era name, only the cyclical year.

sentences.zh: 後三年卒。

translations.literal: Three years later he died.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later he died.

sentences.zh: 承直郎姚邦基者，蜀人也。

translations.literal: Gentleman for Direct Service Yao Bangji was a man of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Bangji, Gentleman for Direct Service, was from Shu.

sentences.zh: 知尉氏縣，秩滿不復仕，屏居村落間，授徒自給。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Weishi; when his term ended he would not serve again but taught in villages for his living.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate of Weishi; when his term ended he taught in villages.

sentences.zh: 時宗室南渡不及者，尚散居民間，豫募人索之，承務郎閻琦匿不以聞，為人所告，豫杖之死。

translations.literal: Many imperial clans who had not crossed south still lived among the people; Yu sought them; Registrar Yan Qi hid them and was reported; Yu beat him to death.
translations.idiomatic: Yu sought stranded imperial kin; Registrar Yan Qi hid them and was beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 劉化源，耀州人。

translations.literal: Liu Huayuan was a man of Yao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Huayuan was from Yao.

sentences.zh: 紹聖元年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi in Shaosheng 1.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi in Shaosheng 1.

sentences.zh: 建炎初，金人陷關陝，守令以城降者，金人因而命之。

translations.literal: Early in Jianyan the Jurchens took Guan and Shaan; prefects and magistrates surrendered and the Jurchens reappointed them.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jianyan the Jurchens took the passes; many officials surrendered and were reappointed.

sentences.zh: 化源時知隴州，不肯降，城陷被執。

translations.literal: Huayuan was then prefect of Long; he would not submit and was seized when the city fell.
translations.idiomatic: Huayuan was prefect of Long; he would not submit and was taken when the city fell.

sentences.zh: 金人使人守之，不得死，遂驅入河北，鬻蔬果、隱民間者十年，終不屈辱。

translations.literal: The Jurchens set guards so he could not die; they drove him to Hebei where for ten years he sold fruit and vegetables among the people and never accepted disgrace.
translations.idiomatic: Guarded so he could not die, he was driven to Hebei; for ten years he sold produce and never bowed.

sentences.zh: 有米璞者，與化源同鄉里，西人皆敬之。

translations.literal: Mi Pu of his home commandery—westerners all honored him.
translations.idiomatic: Mi Pu of his commandery was honored throughout the west.

sentences.zh: 璞登政和二年進士第，時通判原州，劉豫欲官之，杜門謝病，卒不汙偽命。

translations.literal: Pu passed the jinshi in Zhenghe 2; then vice-prefect of Yuan; Liu Yu wished to employ him; he shut his door and pleaded illness, never staining himself with false appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Pu was a Zhenghe 2 jinshi, vice-prefect of Yuan; he refused Liu Yu’s offers and never served the false court.

sentences.zh: 有劉長孺者，亦耀州人。

translations.literal: Liu Changru was also of Yao.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Changru was also from Yao.

sentences.zh: 時簽書博州判官廳公事，與豫書，備陳祖宗德澤，勸以轉禍為福。

translations.literal: Then signing the Bo Prefecture aide’s office; he wrote Yu a letter setting forth ancestral grace and urging him to turn calamity to blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Signing at Bo, he wrote Yu urging him to turn from rebellion to loyalty.

sentences.zh: 豫怒，追其官，囚之百日，長孺終不屈。

translations.literal: Yu was enraged, stripped his office, and imprisoned him a hundred days; Changru never yielded.
translations.idiomatic: Yu imprisoned him a hundred days; Changru never yielded.

sentences.zh: 豫後復官之，不從。

translations.literal: Yu later offered office again; he would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Yu offered office again; he refused.

sentences.zh: 紹興九年，宣諭使周聿上之朝，詔赴行在，而簽書樞密院事樓炤言璞苦風痹，化源、長孺老病，遂命各轉兩官奉祠；

translations.literal: In Shaoxing 9 Commissioner Zhou Yu reported to court; they were ordered to the mobile court; Vice Grand Councilor Lou Zhao said Pu had severe rheumatism and Huayuan and Changru were old and ill—each was given two ranks and a sinecure;
translations.idiomatic: In Shaoxing 9 they were summoned; Lou Zhao cited illness and they received sinecures.

sentences.zh: 又言新鳳翔教授陰卓守節不仕，詔特改令入官。

translations.literal: He also said the new Fengxiang professor Yin Zhuo kept his integrity and would not serve; the throne specially made him a magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Zhuo of Fengxiang, who would not serve, was made a magistrate.

sentences.zh: 其後金復渝盟，長孺知華陰縣，不屈而死。

translations.literal: Later when the Jurchens again broke the treaty, Changru was magistrate of Huayin and died unyielding.
translations.idiomatic: When the treaty broke again, Changru was magistrate of Huayin and died refusing to yield.

sentences.zh: 有李嚞者，開封人。

translations.literal: Li Yan was a man of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yan was from Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 宣和六年進士。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Xuanhe he passed the jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi in Xuanhe 6.

sentences.zh: 建炎中，知彭陽縣，亦不降，與民移治境上。

translations.literal: In Jianyan he was magistrate of Pengyang; he would not submit and moved the government with the people to the border.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianyan he governed Pengyang, would not submit, and moved with the people to the border.

sentences.zh: 令執之以獻，金人欲官之，凡三辭。

translations.literal: He was seized to be presented; the Jurchens wished to give him office; he refused thrice.
translations.idiomatic: Captured, he was offered office thrice and refused.

sentences.zh: 其後金人以為歸附，命為儒林郎，嚞言於所司曰：「昔為俘獲，不敢受歸附之賞。」

translations.literal: Later the Jurchens treated him as having submitted and made him Confucian Gentleman; Yan told the office: “I was once a captive—I dare not take reward for submission.”
translations.idiomatic: They made him Confucian Gentleman; he said: “I was a captive and dare not take submission’s reward.”

sentences.zh: 還其牒。

translations.literal: He returned the document.
translations.idiomatic: He returned the commission.

sentences.zh: 劉麟聞其賢，命張中孚以禮招致，嚞力拒之。

translations.literal: Liu Lin heard his worth and had Zhang Zhongfu invite him with ceremony; Yan firmly refused.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Lin sent Zhang Zhongfu to invite him; Yan refused.

sentences.zh: 紹興九年死原州。

translations.literal: He died at Yuan Prefecture in Shaoxing 9.
translations.idiomatic: He died at Yuan in Shaoxing 9.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈奉議郎，官其家一人。

translations.literal: Reported, he was posthumously made Gentleman for Discussion and one in his family was given office.
translations.idiomatic: The court posthumously made him Gentleman for Discussion and enrolled one kinsman.

sentences.zh: 胡唐老，字俊明，樞密副使宿之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Hu Tanglao, style Junming, was a great-grandson of Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs Su.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Tanglao, style Junming, was a great-grandson of Vice Commissioner Su of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 崇寧間，與弟世將同登進士第。

translations.literal: In the Chongning era he and his younger brother Shijiang passed the jinshi together.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongning he and his brother Shijiang passed the jinshi together.

sentences.zh: 歷南京國子博士，知江陵縣，召為祕書省校書郎。

translations.literal: He served as doctor of the National University at Nanjing, magistrate of Jiangling County, and was summoned as collator in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was a National University doctor at Nanjing, magistrate of Jiangling, then collator in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 靖康元年，擢殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: In Jingkang 1 he was promoted to Attending Censor in the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingkang 1 he became Attending Censor in the Palace.

sentences.zh: 金人再犯京師，攻圍日急，唐老請對曰：「城危矣。

translations.literal: When the Jurchens again attacked the capital and the siege grew daily more urgent, Tanglao requested audience and said: “The city is in peril.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jurchens again besieged the capital, Tanglao said: “The city is in peril.

sentences.zh: 康王北使，為河朔士民留不得進，殆天意也。

translations.literal: The Prince of Kang went north as envoy but was held back by the people of Hebei and could not advance—perhaps heaven’s intent.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Kang was detained in Hebei on his northern mission—perhaps by heaven’s design.

sentences.zh: 請就拜大元帥，俾召天下兵入援。」

translations.literal: Please appoint him Grand Marshal on the spot and have him summon troops from all the realm to relieve us.”
translations.idiomatic: Appoint him Grand Marshal now and summon troops from all the realm.”

sentences.zh: 宰相何㮚是之，遂遣秦仔持蠟書詣相州，拜王河北兵馬大元帥。

translations.literal: Chief Councilor He Li agreed and sent Qin Zai with a sealed letter to Xiang Prefecture to invest the prince as Grand Marshal of Hebei military forces.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Councilor He Li agreed and sent Qin Zai with a sealed letter to Xiang to invest the prince as Grand Marshal of Hebei.

sentences.zh: 時朝廷趣西兵入衛，而不立帥。

translations.literal: The court was urging western troops to guard the capital but appointed no commander.
translations.idiomatic: The court urged western troops to the capital but named no commander.

sentences.zh: 唐老疏：「乞命範致虛為宣撫使，節制諸路以進，不然必無功。」

translations.literal: Tanglao memorialized: “Appoint Fan Zhixu pacification commissioner to command all routes to advance, or there will be no success.”
translations.idiomatic: Hu Tanglao wrote: “Make Fan Zhixu pacification commissioner or there will be no success.”

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: They did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The court did not listen.

sentences.zh: 後致虛以孤軍與金人戰淆、澠間，它路兵不至，遂敗。

translations.literal: Later Zhixu fought the Jurchens alone between Xiao and Mian; other routes’ troops did not come and he was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Later Fan Zhixu fought alone between Xiao and Mian without aid and was defeated.

sentences.zh: 京城破，金人搜括金銀，分命朝臣董之，以台臣糾察，唐老預焉。

translations.literal: When the capital fell the Jurchens searched for gold and silver and assigned court ministers to gather it, with censors to oversee; Tanglao was among them.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital fell Jurchens assigned ministers to gather gold; Tanglao was among them.

sentences.zh: 出知無為軍。

translations.literal: He was made prefect of Wuwei Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was made prefect of Wuwei Army.

sentences.zh: 朝廷竄逐偽命之臣，坐降二官。

translations.literal: The court banished ministers who had taken false appointments; he was demoted two ranks.
translations.idiomatic: The court banished false appointees; he was demoted two ranks.

sentences.zh: 先是，金人怒民間多匿金銀，杖唐老幾死，以疾得免稱臣於偽楚。

translations.literal: Earlier the Jurchens, angry that people hid gold, nearly beat Tanglao to death; by illness he escaped having to bow to the false Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Jurchens nearly beat him to death over hidden gold; illness spared him bowing to false Chu.

sentences.zh: 至是，唐老不自言故，例從貶秩。

translations.literal: Now Tanglao did not explain this and was demoted with the rest.
translations.idiomatic: He did not explain and was demoted with others.

sentences.zh: 三年，知衢州。

translations.literal: In year three he was made prefect of Qu.
translations.idiomatic: In year three he was made prefect of Qu.

sentences.zh: 苗傅敗走，以亂兵犯城，唐老拒之。

translations.literal: Miao Fu fled defeated and mutinous troops attacked the city; Tanglao repelled them.
translations.idiomatic: Miao Fu’s defeated mutineers attacked Qu; Tanglao repelled them.

sentences.zh: 會大雨雹，城上矢石俱發，賊不支，遂解去。

translations.literal: Great hail fell; arrows and stones flew from the walls and the bandits could not stand and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Hail fell; arrows and stones from the walls drove them off.

sentences.zh: 以功擢秘閣修撰，未幾，進徽猷閣待制，充兩浙宣撫司參謀官，知鎮江府兼浙西安撫使。

translations.literal: For merit he was made Compiler of the Secretariat; soon Attendant of the Hall of Imperial Sagacity, staff of the Two-Zhe pacification commission, and prefect of Runzhou with Zhexi pacification.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he became Compiler, then Attendant, and prefect of Run with Zhexi pacification.

sentences.zh: 杜充降於金，建康失守，潰卒戚方等趣鎮江，城壁頹圮，兵不滿千，獨倚浙西製置韓世忠為重。

translations.literal: Du Chong surrendered to the Jurchens; Jiankang fell; broken troops like Qi Fang rushed on Runzhou; walls crumbled and troops were under a thousand—he relied on Han Shizhong of western Zhe as his strength.
translations.idiomatic: When Du Chong surrendered and Jiankang fell, broken troops rushed Runzhou; he had under a thousand men and relied on Han Shizhong.

sentences.zh: 世忠復去，唐老度力不敵，因撫之。

translations.literal: Shizhong left; Tanglao knew he could not resist and soothed them.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhong left; knowing he could not resist, Tanglao soothed the troops.

sentences.zh: 無何，方欲犯臨安，妄言赴行在，請唐老部眾以行。

translations.literal: Soon Fang wished to attack Lin’an, falsely saying he was going to the mobile court and asked Tanglao to march with him.
translations.idiomatic: Fang wished to attack Lin’an, falsely claiming he marched to court, and asked Tanglao to join.

sentences.zh: 唐老不從，諭以逆順禍福，方眾環脅之，唐老怒罵方，遂遇害。

translations.literal: Tanglao refused, explained fortune and ruin, loyalty and treason; Fang’s men surrounded and threatened him; Tanglao cursed Fang and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Tanglao refused, explained loyalty and treason; surrounded, he cursed Fang and was killed.

sentences.zh: 詔贈徽猷閣直學士，諡定湣。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Direct Academician of the Hall of Imperial Sagacity with posthumous name Dingmin.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Direct Academician with the name Dingmin.

sentences.zh: 時安撫司機宜鄭凝之亦以兵死，詔官其家一人。

translations.literal: Staff officer Zheng Ningzhi also died fighting; one in his family was given office.
translations.idiomatic: Staff officer Zheng Ningzhi also fell; one kinsman was enrolled.

sentences.zh: 凝之，戩孫也。

translations.literal: Ningzhi was grandson of Zhan.
translations.idiomatic: Ningzhi was Zhan’s grandson.

sentences.zh: 王儔，以通判真州權通判廣德軍。

translations.literal: Wang Chou, as vice-prefect of Zhen, acted as vice-prefect of Guangde Army.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chou acted as vice-prefect of Guangde.

sentences.zh: 建炎末，盜戚方既為劉晏所破，引兵欲趨宣城，道過廣德，入其郛。

translations.literal: At the end of Jianyan bandit Qi Fang, broken by Liu Yan, marched toward Xuancheng and entered the suburbs of Guangde.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Fang, broken by Liu Yan, entered Guangde’s suburbs.

sentences.zh: 儔不屈，與權判官李唐俊、權司法潘偊、權知廣德縣韋績、權丞蔣夔皆死。

translations.literal: Chou would not submit; with acting judge Li Tangjun, judicial aide Pan Wei, acting magistrate Wei Ji, and aide Jiang Kui all died.
translations.idiomatic: Chou would not submit; Li Tangjun, Pan Wei, Wei Ji, and Jiang Kui died with him.

sentences.zh: 後贈儔二官，唐俊等皆京秩，錄其家一人。

translations.literal: Later Chou was posthumously advanced two ranks; Tangjun and the rest received capital rank; one in each family was enrolled.
translations.idiomatic: Chou was advanced two ranks posthumously; the others received capital rank and one kinsman each.

sentences.zh: 朱嗣孟，饒州樂平人。

translations.literal: Zhu Simeng was a man of Leping in Raozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Simeng was from Leping in Raozhou.

sentences.zh: 宣和間進士，為廣德司戶兼司理。

translations.literal: A jinshi in Xuanhe, he was registrar and judicial officer of Guangde.
translations.idiomatic: A Xuanhe jinshi, he was registrar and judicial officer of Guangde.

sentences.zh: 叛卒戚方破鎮江，犯廣德，守倉皇遣招安，無敢往者，奇嗣孟狀貌有膽略，遂以命焉。

translations.literal: Rebel Qi Fang broke Zhenjiang and attacked Guangde; the prefect hastily sent to negotiate; none dared go; seeing Simeng’s bold bearing they sent him.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi Fang attacked Guangde none dared treat; they sent the bold Simeng.

sentences.zh: 嗣孟雅自負，不復遜，直詣賊壘，問所以涉吾地何故，為陳逆順禍福，使自擇所處。

translations.literal: Simeng was proud and did not defer; he went straight to the camp, asked why they trespassed, explained loyalty and treason, and bade them choose.
translations.idiomatic: Proud, he went to the camp, asked their purpose, explained loyalty, and bade them choose.

sentences.zh: 方以迕己殺之。

translations.literal: Fang killed him for defiance.
translations.idiomatic: Fang killed him for defying him.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈宣教郎，官其子。

translations.literal: Reported, he was posthumously made Instructor of the Court and his son was given office.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Instructor and his son enrolled.

sentences.zh: 劉晏，字平甫，嚴州人。

translations.literal: Liu Yan, style Pingfu, was a man of Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yan, style Pingfu, was from Yan.

sentences.zh: 入遼，舉進士，為尚書郎。

translations.literal: He entered Liao, passed the jinshi, and was a secretary in the Ministry.
translations.idiomatic: He entered Liao, passed its jinshi, and served in the Ministry.

sentences.zh: 宣和四年，帥眾數百來歸，授通直郎。

translations.literal: In Xuanhe 4 he led several hundred men to submit and was made Gentleman for Direct Communication.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuanhe 4 he submitted with hundreds of men and was made Gentleman for Direct Communication.

sentences.zh: 金人犯京師，以晏總遼東兵，號「赤心隊」。

translations.literal: When the Jurchens attacked the capital Yan commanded Liaodong troops called the “Red-Heart Company.”
translations.idiomatic: When the Jurchens attacked the capital he led Liaodong troops called the "Red-Heart Company."

sentences.zh: 建炎初，從劉正彥擊淮西賊丁進。

translations.literal: Early in Jianyan he followed Liu Zhengyan against the Huai bandit Ding Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jianyan he followed Liu Zhengyan against Ding Jin.

sentences.zh: 進黨頗眾，晏所提赤心騎才八百，乃為五色旗，使騎兵持之，循山而出，一色盡則以一色易之。

translations.literal: Jin’s party was large; Yan had only eight hundred Red-Heart horsemen; he made five-colored banners so cavalry bore them in rotation from the hills—when one color ended they changed—and the bandits, seeing government troops unending for days, surrendered without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: With only eight hundred horsemen he rotated five-colored banners from the hills until the bandits surrendered.

sentences.zh: 賊見官軍累日不絕，顏色各異，遂不戰而降。

translations.literal: Seeing government troops unending for days with banners of different colors, the bandits surrendered without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing endless government troops with shifting banner colors, the bandits surrendered without a fight.

sentences.zh: 遷朝散郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Gentleman for Court Discussion.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Gentleman for Court Discussion.

sentences.zh: 正彥反，晏謂其部曲曰：「吾豈從逆黨者耶？」

translations.literal: When Zhengyan rebelled, Yan said to his followers: "Would I follow rebels?"
translations.idiomatic: When Zhengyan rebelled, Yan said to his followers: "Would I follow rebels?"

sentences.zh: 以眾歸韓世忠。

translations.literal: He brought his forces to Han Shizhong.
translations.idiomatic: He brought his forces to Han Shizhong.

sentences.zh: 世忠追正彥及苗傅於浦城，以晏騎六百為疑兵於浦山之陽，賊大駭，晏以所部力戰。

translations.literal: When Zhengyan was taken, Shizhong reported his merit and he was advanced one rank.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhengyan was captured, Yan was advanced one rank.

sentences.zh: 正彥既擒，世忠上其功，遷一官。

translations.literal: When the Jurchens attacked Jiankang and Du Chong’s army broke, Shizhong withdrew to Jiangyin; Yan camped at Qinglong with a hundred fifty Red-Heart horse.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiankang fell, Yan camped at Qinglong with a hundred fifty horse.

sentences.zh: 金人犯建康，杜充兵潰，世忠退保江陰，晏領赤心百五十騎屯青龍。

translations.literal: Bandits attacked Changzhou; the prefect begged Yan’s aid; with seven thousand picked men he surprised and broke them.
translations.idiomatic: He relieved Changzhou with seven thousand picked men.

sentences.zh: 群寇犯常州，郡守請晏為援，晏以精銳七千人出奇破之。

translations.literal: He was made Direct Academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Direct Academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall.

sentences.zh: 進直龍圖閣。

translations.literal: He held Maji Mountain against bandits; when they came again he chose river troops to fight, accepting fifteen hundred surrendering; the prefecture built a living shrine to Yan.
translations.idiomatic: He held Maji Mountain, accepted fifteen hundred surrendering, and the people built him a living shrine.

sentences.zh: 保馬跡山以捍寇，寇再至，晏選舟師迎戰，降其眾千五百人，郡人為晏立生祠。

translations.literal: Qi Fang besieged Xuancheng; Yan was urgently ordered; he reached the wall, and before camp was set struck Fang’s tent; Fang fled in shock.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to relieve Xuancheng, he struck Fang’s tent before making camp and Fang fled.

sentences.zh: 戚方圍宣城，急命晏往援，晏至城下，未立營壘，出不意直搗方帳下，方大驚卻走。

translations.literal: Yan wished to take Fang alive; alone he pursued; Fang turned with his host; Yan could not match them but still killed dozens and was slain by bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuing alone to capture Fang, he was overwhelmed but killed dozens before he fell.

sentences.zh: 晏欲生致方，單騎追之，方率其眾迎戰，晏不能敵，猶手殺數十人，為賊所害。

translations.literal: Reported, he was posthumously made Attendant of the Dragon Diagram Hall; four sons were given office; a temple at the place of death was named Righteous Fierceness and sacrificed yearly.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously Attendant of the Dragon Diagram; four sons enrolled; a temple named Righteous Fierceness.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈龍圖閣待制，官其子四人，於死所立廟曰義烈，歲時祀之。

translations.literal: Zheng Zhen, style Xiongshu, was a man of Xianyou in Xinghua.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Zhen, style Xiongshu, was from Xianyou in Xinghua.

sentences.zh: 鄭振，字亨叔，興化軍仙遊人。

translations.literal: In Jianyan bandit Yang rose; the magistrate ordered Zhen to gather militia.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianyan he gathered militia against Yang.

sentences.zh: 建炎中，盜楊步勍起，邑令檄振糾集民兵以禦之。

translations.literal: In Jianyan bandit Yang Buqiong rose; the magistrate ordered Zhen to gather militia to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianyan the bandit Yang Buqiong rose; the magistrate ordered Zhen to gather militia against him.

sentences.zh: 振力戰，賊眾披靡，一夕遁去。

translations.literal: In Shaoxing 13 bandits Zeng Shaolong, Zhou Laolong, He Baiqi, and Chen Dadao came in tens of thousands; the command ordered Zhen out; the bandits had heard his name and submitted without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaoxing 13 great bandit hosts came; hearing Zhen’s name they submitted.

sentences.zh: 紹興十三年，群盜曾少龍、周老龍、何白旗、陳大刀眾至數萬，帥司檄振行，盜素聞振名，不戰自屈。

translations.literal: In year 16 bandit Zhan Tieyi entered his well and lane; Zhen led the crowd to resist, killed dozens, and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: In year 16 Zhan Tieyi entered his village; he resisted, killed dozens, and died.

sentences.zh: 十六年，盜詹鐵義者，入振井裏，振帥眾拒之，殺數十人，遂遇害。

translations.literal: A temple sacrifice was kept in the village.
translations.idiomatic: The village kept a temple to him.

sentences.zh: 廟食里中。

translations.literal: His grandson Zhiwei was Gentleman for Court Service and vice-prefect of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Zhiwei was vice-prefect of Shu.

sentences.zh: 有孫知微者，以朝請大夫通判舒州。

translations.literal: In Shaoxing 1 bandit Liu Zhong entered the border, seized Zhiwei, and took him away; Zhiwei would not yield; Zhong in rage dismembered and ate him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhong seized Zhiwei, who would not yield; Zhong dismembered and ate him.

sentences.zh: 紹興元年，賊劉忠入其境，執知微以去，知微不屈，忠怒，臠而食之。

translations.literal: Meng Yanqing was a cousin of Zhonghou and knew warfare.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Yanqing was Zhonghou’s cousin and knew warfare.

sentences.zh: 孟彥卿，忠厚從父也，頗知兵。

translations.literal: Vice-prefect of Tan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was vice-prefect of Tan.

sentences.zh: 通判潭州。

translations.literal: In Jianyan 3 mutinous soldiers in Tan burned and plundered and left by the east gate; Commander Xiang Ziyun ordered Yanqing to pursue.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianyan 3 mutineers left Tan; Xiang Ziyun ordered Yanqing to pursue.

sentences.zh: 建炎三年，潭城中叛卒焚掠，自東門出，帥臣向子諲命彥卿領兵追之。

translations.literal: Soon they were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: They were soon pacified.

sentences.zh: 已而招安其眾。

translations.literal: Before long broken troops under Du Yan from Yuan entered Liuyang and attacked Shanhua and Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yan’s broken troops from Yuan attacked Changsha.

sentences.zh: 未幾，潰兵杜彥自袁州入瀏陽，遂犯善化、長沙二縣。

translations.literal: Yanqing led militia to resist, personally killed several, and the bandits’ momentum broke and they returned to Liuyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqing led militia, killed several, and drove them back.

sentences.zh: 彥卿率民兵拒之，手殺數人，賊勢挫，退還瀏陽。

translations.literal: Yanqing led militia to resist, personally killed several men, the bandits' momentum broke, and they withdrew to Liuyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqing led militia to resist, killed several with his own hand, and drove the bandits back to Liuyang.

sentences.zh: 彥卿追與之戰。

translations.literal: Yanqing pursued and fought them.
translations.idiomatic: He pursued and fought them.

sentences.zh: 俄而民兵有自潰者，賊遂乘之，斬彥卿，持其首以告所掠民兵曰：「此善戰孟通判首也。」

translations.literal: Soon some militia broke on their own; the bandits pressed the advantage, beheaded Yanqing, and holding up his head told the captured militia: "This is the head of Vice-Prefect Meng, so fierce in battle."
translations.idiomatic: When some militia broke, the bandits beheaded Yanqing and told the captives: "This is the head of Vice-Prefect Meng, so fierce in battle."

sentences.zh: 因支解以徇。

translations.literal: They then dismembered him to warn others.
translations.idiomatic: They dismembered him as a warning.

sentences.zh: 添差通判趙民彥以民兵赴之，鏖戰瀏陽城南南流橋，依山為陣，殺傷甚眾。

translations.literal: By chance a spy broke his identifying banner in the ranks; the crowd feared Minyan had fallen and broke; Minyan was taken.
translations.idiomatic: A spy broke his banner; troops thought him dead and broke; Minyan was taken.

sentences.zh: 偶為間者折其陣中認旗，眾驚謂民彥已敗，遂潰，民彥為賊所得。

translations.literal: Local gentleman Xie Chun, brave and able, was chosen to lead militia as vanguard with Minyan.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Chun led militia as vanguard with Minyan.

sentences.zh: 邑士謝淳以才勇，眾推之帥民兵為前鋒，助民彥戰。

translations.literal: Chun personally killed dozens; strength failed and he was seized.
translations.idiomatic: Chun killed dozens before he was seized.

sentences.zh: 淳手殺數十人，力屈亦被執。

translations.literal: The bandits killed them both.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits killed them both.

sentences.zh: 賊並殺之。

translations.literal: Reported, Yanqing and Minyan were each posthumously made Direct Academicians of the Dragon Diagram Hall and three in each family were enrolled.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqing and Minyan were posthumously made Direct Academicians; three kin each enrolled.

sentences.zh: 事聞，彥卿、民彥並贈直龍圖閣，官其家各三人。

translations.literal: Chun, style Jingxiang, was posthumously made Gentleman for Martial Loyalty; his son Xigu was given office.
translations.idiomatic: Chun was posthumously made Gentleman for Martial Loyalty; his son enrolled.

sentences.zh: 淳字景祥，贈成忠郎，官其子晞古。

translations.literal: Zhu Xi as Hunan commander asked temples for Yanqing and Minyan with Chun as associate.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xi asked temples for Yanqing and Minyan with Chun beside them.

sentences.zh: 朱熹帥湖南，請為彥卿、民彥立廟，以淳侑之。

translations.literal: Gao Tan, style Jingsui, was a man of Guangze in Shaowu.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Tan, style Jingsui, was from Guangze in Shaowu.

sentences.zh: 高談字景遂，邵武光澤人。

translations.literal: In Shaoding 2 bandits rose in neighboring prefectures; his sons asked him to flee; Tan said: “Formerly Yang Zixun asked Hu An’guo how to flee bandits; he said: ‘In past years when bandits rose in Yanshan, Hebei and Guanzhong could be fled to; entering the passes, Huainan and Hannan could be fled to; now only the two Guang—can we be sure they will have no bandits? I can only set my heart and await fate.’ Young man, remember—this is a maxim.”
translations.idiomatic: When bandits rose nearby his sons begged flight; he quoted Hu An’guo: only the two Guang remained—and one must await fate.

sentences.zh: 紹定二年，旁郡盜作，諸子請避之，談曰：「昔楊子訓問避寇於胡文定公，語之曰：『往歲盜起燕山，則河北、關中可避；

translations.literal: In Shaoding 2, bandits arose in neighboring commanderies, and Tan's sons asked to flee. Tan said: "Formerly Yang Zixun asked Hu Wending where to avoid bandits, and Hu told him: 'In past years bandits arose at Yanshan, so Hebei and Guanzhong could be avoided;
translations.idiomatic: In Shaoding 2, bandits rose in nearby commanderies, and Tan's sons urged him to flee. Tan said, "Long ago Yang Zixun asked Hu Wending where one might escape bandits, and Hu replied: 'In past years, when bandits rose at Yanshan, Hebei and Guanzhong could be avoided;

sentences.zh: 入關，則淮南、漢南可避；

translations.literal: if they entered the passes, then Huainan and Hannan could be avoided;
translations.idiomatic: if they entered the passes, Huainan and Hannan might serve;

sentences.zh: 今惟二廣，寧保其無寇乎？

translations.literal: now only the two Guang remain; can we be sure they will have no bandits?
translations.idiomatic: now only the two Guang remain; can we be sure they will have no raiders?

sentences.zh: 吾惟存心以聽命爾。』

translations.literal: I can only preserve my heart and await the command.'
translations.idiomatic: I can only keep my resolve and await orders.'

sentences.zh: 小子識之，此格言也。

translations.literal: Young men, remember this; it is a maxim.
translations.idiomatic: Remember this, young men; it is a maxim.

sentences.zh: 今南去則汀、劍，西去則盱、贛，皆為盜區；

translations.literal: Now if we go south, Ting and Jian, and if we go west, Xu and Gan, are all bandit zones;
translations.idiomatic: Now south lies Ting and Jian, and west Xu and Gan—all bandit country;

sentences.zh: 東去富、沙，雖有城避，吾聞官吏例弗我納；

translations.literal: if we go east to Fu and Sha, though there are cities to shelter in, I hear the officials as a rule will not take us in;
translations.idiomatic: east to Fu and Sha there are walled cities, but I hear the officials generally will not admit us;

sentences.zh: 北去廣信，防夫、守隸利人囊篋，指民為諜，數剽殺之。

translations.literal: if we go north to Guangxin, guards and clerks covet travelers' bags, call the people spies, and repeatedly rob and kill them.
translations.idiomatic: north to Guangxin, guards covet travelers' baggage and kill people as spies.

sentences.zh: 舍胡公之言未有他策也。」

translations.literal: Apart from Master Hu's words, there is no other plan."
translations.idiomatic: Apart from Master Hu's words, we have no other plan."

sentences.zh: 盜入，諸子又請，談曰：「有廟祏在，將焉之？」

translations.literal: When bandits entered, his sons again asked to flee. Tan said: "The temple tablets are here—where would we go?"
translations.idiomatic: When bandits came, his sons asked again. Tan said, "The ancestral tablets are here—where would we go?"

sentences.zh: 盜至，談出曰：「時和歲豐，何忍為此？」

translations.literal: Bandits said: “Officials are greedy and violent; the people have nowhere to appeal—we act to right it.”
translations.idiomatic: Bandits said: “Officials are cruel; we right the people’s wrongs.”

sentences.zh: 盜曰：「 吏貪暴，民無所訴，我為直之。」

translations.literal: Bandits said: “Officials are greedy and violent; the people have nowhere to appeal—we act to right it.”
translations.idiomatic: The bandits said: “Officials are cruel; the people have no recourse—we set things right.”

sentences.zh: 談曰：「獨不能楇鼓上聞乎？

translations.literal: Tan said: “Can you not beat the drum and report to the throne?
translations.idiomatic: Tan said: “Why not beat the drum and report upward?

sentences.zh: 民何辜而殺之。」

translations.literal: What guilt have the people that you kill them.”
translations.idiomatic: What crime have the people committed that you kill them?”

sentences.zh: 盜怒，執諸庭。

translations.literal: Bandits were enraged and seized him in the courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits were enraged and seized him in the court.

sentences.zh: 遺之牛酒，不釋；

translations.literal: They sent oxen and wine—he would not be released;
translations.idiomatic: They offered oxen and wine—he would not yield;

sentences.zh: 遺之金帛，不釋。

translations.literal: they sent gold and silk—he would not be released.
translations.idiomatic: they offered gold and silk—he would not yield.

sentences.zh: 談曰：「然則將何為？」

translations.literal: Tan said: “Then what do you want?”
translations.idiomatic: Tan said: “Then what do you want?”

sentences.zh: 盜曰：「我欲東破武陽，若得耆老如爾者，率是鄉子弟，吾其濟乎。」

translations.literal: Bandits said: “I wish to break Wuyang to the east; if I get elders like you to lead the township youth, I may succeed.”
translations.idiomatic: The bandits said: “We mean to strike Wuyang—elders like you could lead the local youth.”

sentences.zh: 談曰：「斯言奚為至我。」

translations.literal: Tan said: “Why bring such words to me?”
translations.idiomatic: Tan said: “Why say this to me?”

sentences.zh: 唾賊大罵，遂遇害，而里人賴以免。

translations.literal: He spat, cursed the bandits fiercely, and was killed; the village was spared because of him.
translations.idiomatic: He spat, cursed them fiercely, and was killed; the village was spared through him.

sentences.zh: 談平居言動，必由禮法，故鄉人敬而附之。

translations.literal: In daily life Tan’s words and acts followed ritual; townspeople honored and followed him.
translations.idiomatic: In daily life his words and acts followed ritual, and neighbors honored and followed him.

sentences.zh: 連萬夫，德安人，或曰南夫弟也。

translations.literal: Lian Wanfu of De’an—some say younger brother of Nanfu.
translations.idiomatic: Lian Wanfu of De’an—some say he was Nanfu’s younger brother.

sentences.zh: 補將仕郎。

translations.literal: By supplement he was Gentleman for Initial Service.
translations.idiomatic: By supplement he was made Gentleman for Initial Service.

sentences.zh: 建炎四年，群賊犯應山，萬夫率邑人數千保山砦，賊不能犯。

translations.literal: In Jianyan 4 bandits attacked Yingshan; Wanfu led thousands of townspeople to hold a mountain fort; bandits could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianyan 4 he led thousands of townspeople to a mountain fort at Yingshan that bandits could not take.

sentences.zh: 寇浪子者以兵至，圍之三日，卒破之。

translations.literal: Bandit Langzi came with troops, besieged three days, and broke through.
translations.idiomatic: The bandit Langzi besieged three days and broke in.

sentences.zh: 賊知萬夫勇敢有謀，欲留為用，萬夫怒，厲聲罵賊，為所害。

translations.literal: Knowing Wanfu was brave and shrewd, they wished to keep him; Wanfu cursed fiercely and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Wishing to keep the brave and shrewd Wanfu, they killed him when he cursed them.

sentences.zh: 贈右承務郎，官其家一人。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Gentleman for the Right Secretariat and one in his family was given office.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Gentleman for the Right Secretariat; one kinsman was enrolled.

sentences.zh: 謝皐者，開封人，為鎮撫司統制官。

translations.literal: Xie Gao was a man of Kaifeng, overall controller of the Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Gao of Kaifeng was overall controller of the Pacification Commission.

sentences.zh: 李成陷虢州，欲降之，皋指腹示賊曰：「此吾赤心也。」

translations.literal: When Li Cheng took Guo Prefecture and wished to induce him, Gao pointed to his belly: “This is my red heart.”
translations.idiomatic: When Li Cheng took Guo and wished to win him, Gao pointed to his belly: “This is my red heart.”

sentences.zh: 自剖其心以死。

translations.literal: He cut open his own heart and died.
translations.idiomatic: He cut out his own heart and died.

sentences.zh: 王大壽，泉州人，為左翼隊將。

translations.literal: Wang Dashou of Quan was a captain of the Left Wing.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dashou of Quan was a captain of the Left Wing.

sentences.zh: 紹定五年，海寇王子清犯圍頭，守真德秀遣大壽領卒百人防遏。

translations.literal: In Shaoding 5 sea bandit Wang Ziqing attacked Weitou; Prefect Zhen Dexiu sent Dashou with a hundred men to block them.
translations.idiomatic: In Shaoding 5 Prefect Zhen Dexiu sent him with a hundred men against sea bandit Wang Ziqing at Weitou.

sentences.zh: 猝與賊遇，奮前控弦，斃賊十餘，後無援者，遂沒。

translations.literal: Suddenly meeting the bandits he charged forward, drew the bow, killed more than ten; with no reinforcements he perished.
translations.idiomatic: He met the bandits suddenly, killed more than ten with his bow, and perished without reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 從死者五人。

translations.literal: Five who followed him died.
translations.idiomatic: Five who followed him also died.

sentences.zh: 賊就俘，剖心祭之。

translations.literal: When the bandits were captured they cut out hearts to sacrifice to him.
translations.idiomatic: When the bandits were captured they cut out hearts to sacrifice to him.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈官，恤其家。

translations.literal: Reported, he was posthumously advanced and his family comforted.
translations.idiomatic: The court posthumously advanced him and comforted his family.

sentences.zh: 薛良顯，字貴勤，溫之瑞安人。

translations.literal: Xue Liangxian, style Guiqin, was a man of Rui’an in Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Liangxian, style Guiqin, was from Rui’an in Wen.

sentences.zh: 登崇寧二年進士第，累官為大宗正丞，出為江東轉運使。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi in Chongning 2, rose to Director of the Imperial Clan Court, and went out as transport commissioner of Jiangdong.
translations.idiomatic: A Chongning 2 jinshi, he became director of the Imperial Clan Court and Jiangdong transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 江寧軍校周德作亂，良顯聞變，率眾與戰，斬十餘級，力不勝，死之。

translations.literal: A garrison officer of Jiangning, Zhou De, rebelled; Liangxian heard, led troops to fight, cut more than ten heads, strength failed, and he died.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou De rebelled at Jiangning he led troops, beheaded more than ten, and died when strength failed.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈恤良渥。

translations.literal: Reported, generous posthumous rewards were given.
translations.idiomatic: The court gave generous posthumous rewards.

sentences.zh: 唐敏求，字好古，太平當塗人。

translations.literal: Tang Minqiu, style Haogu, was a man of Dangtu in Taiping.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Minqiu, style Haogu, was from Dangtu in Taiping.

sentences.zh: 宣和六年進士，調德化主簿。

translations.literal: A jinshi in Xuanhe 6, he was appointed chief magistrate of Dehua.
translations.idiomatic: A Xuanhe 6 jinshi, he was chief magistrate of Dehua.

sentences.zh: 盜起，敏求挺身率眾捍賊，度力不能支，諭以禍福，賊憤詆觸，噪而前，遂遇害。

translations.literal: Bandits rose; Minqiu led the crowd to resist; seeing strength would not hold, he explained fortune and ruin; the bandits raged and cursed and rushed forward, and he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits rose he led resistance; seeing he could not hold, he reasoned with them; enraged, they rushed and killed him.

sentences.zh: 事聞，加贈升朝官，仍補其子楠將仕郎。

translations.literal: Reported, he was posthumously advanced to court rank and his son Nan was made Gentleman for Initial Service.
translations.idiomatic: The court posthumously advanced him and made his son Nan Gentleman for Initial Service.

sentences.zh: 王師道，字居中，兗州人。

translations.literal: Wang Shidao, style Juzhong, was a man of Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shidao, style Juzhong, was from Yan.

sentences.zh: 為人沈勇。

translations.literal: He was deep and brave.
translations.idiomatic: He was resolute and brave.

sentences.zh: 任吉州栗傳砦巡檢。

translations.literal: He served as inspector of Lituan Stockade in Ji.
translations.idiomatic: He was inspector of Lituan Stockade in Ji.

sentences.zh: 紹興中，與盜戰於吳村，每射輒斃，追擊數里，遇賊有伏於民居者，挺身力戰，遂死。

translations.literal: In Shaoxing he fought bandits at Wu Village; every shot killed; he pursued several li; bandits lay in ambush in houses; he fought fiercely alone and died.
translations.idiomatic: At Wu Village every shot killed; pursuing several li he was ambushed in houses and died fighting.

sentences.zh: 立廟其地。

translations.literal: A temple was built on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: A temple was built on the spot.

sentences.zh: 部使者以聞，官其二子。

translations.literal: The regional commissioner reported it and two sons were given office.
translations.idiomatic: The regional commissioner reported it and two sons were enrolled.

sentences.zh: 王輝者，青州人。

translations.literal: Wang Hui was a man of Qing.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hui was from Qing.

sentences.zh: 亦嘗為栗傳砦巡檢。

translations.literal: He too had been inspector of Lituan Stockade.
translations.idiomatic: He had also been inspector of Lituan Stockade.

sentences.zh: 靖康初，詔起義兵，輝應募，立奇功，官至正使，寓吉州。

translations.literal: At the start of Jingkang an edict called for loyal troops; Hui answered, won strange merit, rose to Regular Commander, and lived in Ji.
translations.idiomatic: At Jingkang he answered the call for loyal troops, won remarkable merit, rose to Regular Commander, and lived in Ji.

sentences.zh: 淳熙二年，茶寇犯邑，郡以輝驍勇，檄之使行。

translations.literal: In Chunxi 2 tea bandits attacked the county; the prefecture, knowing Hui’s valor, ordered him out.
translations.idiomatic: In Chunxi 2 tea bandits attacked the county; the prefecture sent the valiant Hui.

sentences.zh: 至勝鄉，地險，輝勇於進，士卒不繼，為賊所得，以刃加頸欲全之，輝含血大罵，遂死。

translations.literal: At Sheng Village the ground was narrow; Hui pressed forward boldly; troops did not follow and bandits seized him; blades at his neck they wished to spare him; Hui spat blood and cursed and died.
translations.idiomatic: At Sheng Village he charged boldly; unsupported, he was seized; they offered to spare him; he spat blood, cursed, and died.

sentences.zh: 帥司以聞，贈忠州刺史，與恩澤二人，立廟羅陂。

translations.literal: The command reported it; he was posthumously made Prefect of Loyalty; two received grace; a temple was built at Luopo.
translations.idiomatic: The command reported it; he was posthumously made Prefect of Loyalty; two received favor; a temple was built at Luopo.

sentences.zh: 陳霖者，字傅容，泉州人。

translations.literal: Chen Lin, style Furong, was a man of Quan.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Lin, style Furong, was from Quan.

sentences.zh: 嘉定十三年進士，為瑞金尉。

translations.literal: A jinshi in Jiading 13, he was sheriff of Ruijin.
translations.idiomatic: A Jiading 13 jinshi, he was sheriff of Ruijin.

sentences.zh: 盜起江、閩，霖迎敵力戰，盜係之以去，不屈遇害。

translations.literal: Bandits rose on the Jiang and Min; Lin met them and fought hard; bandits bound him and took him away; he would not yield and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits rose on the Jiang and Min he fought hard; seized and bound, he would not yield and was killed.
